help-block-header.title: Header
help-block-header.summary: The top bar of the screen — the Back and Skip buttons and the progress indicator that shows how far along the visitor is.

fields.label: Back Button Label
fields.description: Sets the text and styling of the Back control that returns visitors to the previous step. Defaults to a left arrow and supports other languages. Keep it small so it doesn't compete with your main action, and clear it to hide the button on the first screen, where there's nowhere to go back to.

fields.label: Skip Button Label
fields.description: Sets the text and styling of the Skip control that lets visitors bypass this step. Defaults to 'SKIP' and supports other languages. Use it only where skipping is fine, and clear it to hide it on your paywall and key question screens, where an easy out lowers both sales and the answers you collect.

fields.label: Progress Bar Style
fields.description: Chooses how progress through the funnel looks: a single continuous bar (Line) or segmented dots (Dashes), each with its own color controls below. A visible 'how far along' cue reassures visitors only a few steps remain, which lifts completion. Pick whichever fits your brand and keep it the same across screens.

fields.label: Completed Progress Color
fields.description: Colors the filled, completed part of the progress bar. Defaults to gold for the Line style and teal for Dashes. Use your brand accent and make sure it clearly stands out against the unfilled track color so visitors can see at a glance how far they've come.

fields.label: Remaining Progress Color
fields.description: Colors the empty, not-yet-completed part of the progress bar. Defaults to white for the Line style and light gray for Dashes. Keep it muted next to the filled color so the completed portion clearly reads as progress rather than blending in.

fields.label: Progress Bar Text
fields.description: Optional text shown with the progress bar, such as a 'Step 5 of 10' counter or a short line of reassurance. Supports other languages and styling; leave it empty for a clean bar-only look. Note this text is fixed per screen and won't count up on its own, so use it as a label unless you drive it from a variable.

fields.label: Optional Header Icon
fields.description: Adds an optional small icon, often a logo or step glyph, next to the progress bar, with controls for the image, its size, and its spacing. Most funnels leave this off. Use it only to reinforce branding in the header, and keep the icon small so it doesn't crowd the progress bar.

fields.label: Progress Content Side
fields.description: Sets where the icon and label sit across the header, on the left (Start), centered, or on the right (End). Mostly a cosmetic touch: centered usually looks balanced, while left or right lets you line the label up with your Back or Skip button. Adjust only if the default looks off.

fields.label: Stretch Progress Edge-To-Edge
fields.description: When on, the progress bar stretches all the way across the header; when off, it takes only the width its content needs. Use full width for a bold, obvious progress bar across the top of the screen. Turn it off when you want the bar compact and grouped with a label or icon.

fields.label: Keep Progress Clear Of Buttons
fields.description: When on, which is the default, the progress bar shrinks so it never overlaps the Back or Skip buttons; when off, it can collide with them in a tight header. Leave it on. Turn it off only if you've removed those buttons and want the bar to use the full width.

fields.label: Progress Height In Header
fields.description: Sets where the progress bar sits up and down within the header: at the top, centered, or at the bottom. Centered is the usual balanced choice; use bottom to sit it just above your content, or top to hug the status bar. Adjust only if the default placement looks off for your header height.

fields.label: Header Bar Height
fields.description: Sets how tall the header bar is, from 20 to 200 pixels, with a default of 44, which is the space its buttons and progress bar share. Keep it near the default for a standard bar and raise it only if you add a tall icon or larger text. Going too small cramps the Back and Skip buttons and makes them hard to tap.

fields.label: Header Bar Background
fields.description: Fills the header bar with a color, or clear it to transparent so the screen background shows through for a floating header. Use a solid color to set the header apart from busy content. If you go transparent over a photo or video, check that the Back, Skip, and progress colors still stand out clearly.

fields.label: Header See-Through Level
fields.description: Fades the whole header bar from fully solid to fully see-through, defaulting to solid. Lower it for a soft, partly transparent header that blends into a photo or video background. Keep it high enough that the Back, Skip, and progress controls stay easy to see.

fields.label: Spacing inside the header
fields.description: Sets the inner spacing on each side (top, right, bottom, left) that pushes the Back button, Skip button, and progress bar away from the header edges. Raise the top value to keep these controls clear of the phone's status bar or notch, and adjust left/right so buttons aren't jammed against the screen edge. Start from the defaults and nudge only where something looks cramped, since a clean header keeps the first impression of your ad landing page tidy.

fields.label: Spacing around the progress bar
fields.description: Sets the spacing on each side of the progress indicator alone, separate from the header's overall padding. Use it to fine-tune the gap around the bar, for example to nudge it down from the buttons, without moving the buttons themselves. Most funnels keep the default; adjust only when the bar sits too tight or too loose against the header.

fields.label: Back button text style
fields.description: Overrides how the Back control's label looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, line height, an optional highlight behind the text, and a strikethrough color. By default it inherits your project theme, which keeps every screen consistent. Touch this only when the Back label needs to match a specific header treatment, and keep it subtle so it never competes with your main action.

By default it inherits your theme. Use it to make the reassurance text legible against your header background, and keep it small so it supports rather than overshadows the progress bar.

fields.label: Header icon settings
fields.description: Controls the optional header icon shown next to the progress bar — its image (upload or URL), placement relative to the label, scale mode, width, height, corner rounding, and padding. Off by default. Turn it on only to reinforce branding in the header, and keep the icon small so it doesn't crowd the progress bar or the Back and Skip buttons.

leaves.label: Enable icon
leaves.description: Off by default. Turn on to show a small image (for example a logo) in the header next to the progress indicator; off for no image.

leaves.label: Icon image
leaves.description: Upload an image file or paste an image URL — the icon shown in the header. Leave empty to show no graphic.

leaves.label: Placement
leaves.description: Where the icon sits relative to the progress title: Start (before it) or End (after it); the Fixed Start/End variants pin it to the header’s left/right edge; Top and Bottom stack it above or below.

leaves.label: Scale mode
leaves.description: How the image fits its box: Scale to Fill (stretch), Aspect Fit (show the whole icon, may letterbox), Aspect Fill (cover the box, may crop), or Center (no resize).

leaves.label: Width
leaves.description: The icon’s width in pixels (0–200).

leaves.label: Height
leaves.description: The icon’s height in pixels (0–200).

leaves.label: Corner radius
leaves.description: Rounding of the icon’s corners in pixels; raise it to clip a square image into a rounded or circular badge.

leaves.label: Icon padding
leaves.description: The space around the icon (top, right, bottom, left) — the gap between the icon and the surrounding header content.

help-content-hero.title: Content
help-content-hero.summary: The headline, subtitle, and optional hero image — the words and lead visual that carry the screen.

fields.label: Your main headline
fields.description: The title is the biggest, first thing a visitor reads, so it carries most of the weight on whether they keep going. Turn it on, then write one short benefit-led line, like an ad headline rather than a sentence. Type @ to drop in an earlier answer (for example @user_goal) so it feels personal, and style it under the gear icon below.

fields.label: Write the headline text
fields.description: This is where you type the actual headline; keep it short and benefit-driven. Type @ to pull in a visitor's earlier answer (such as @user_goal) for personalization, add a link inside the text with @link, or insert a countdown with @countdown to create urgency on offer screens. If your funnel runs in more than one language, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

fields.label: Title look and emphasis
fields.description: Override how the headline looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and an optional highlight behind the text. By default it inherits your project theme, which keeps every screen consistent, so most funnels never need to touch this. Override only when one screen needs extra punch, like a bigger color headline on your hero.

leaves.label: Text background color
leaves.description: An optional fill drawn behind the title text (a highlight pill). Off unless you set it; leave empty for plain text on the screen background.

leaves.label: Font family
leaves.description: The typeface of the title.

leaves.label: Line height
leaves.description: Vertical spacing between lines of text — raise it to give multi-line text more breathing room.

leaves.label: Font size
leaves.description: Text size of the title in pixels.

leaves.label: Font weight
leaves.description: How bold the text is, from Thin through Bold to Black.

leaves.label: Text color
leaves.description: The color of the title text. Keep enough contrast with the background that it stays readable.

leaves.label: Text align
leaves.description: Horizontal alignment of the text: start (left), center, or end (right).

leaves.label: Strikethrough color
leaves.description: Color of a line-through decoration when the text is struck out (for example, an old price).

leaves.label: Background opacity
leaves.description: How see-through the text background fill is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid). Only matters when a background color is set.

leaves.label: Background radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding (px) of the text background fill; higher is softer.

fields.label: Space around the title
fields.description: Adds empty space on each side of the title (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't cramped against the screen edges or the text below. Leave it at the theme default unless the title feels too tight or too far from the next element. Increase a side to give it room, or decrease to pull elements closer together.

fields.label: The line under your title
fields.description: The subtitle is the supporting line beneath your title; use it to expand the promise, add proof, or hint at what happens next. Turn it on and keep it to one short sentence; it shows smaller and lighter than the title by default so the headline stays dominant. Like the title, you can personalize it with @ variables. Skip it on screens where the title already says everything.

fields.label: Write the subtitle text
fields.description: Type the supporting line that sits under your title here, one short sentence that reinforces the offer or tells the visitor what comes next. The same shortcuts work as in the title: type @ to insert an earlier answer, @link to add a clickable link, or @countdown for urgency. If your funnel is multilingual, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

fields.label: Subtitle look and emphasis
fields.description: Change how the subtitle looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and an optional background — styled separately from the title so you can tune each one. By default it inherits your theme (usually smaller and lighter than the title), which works for most funnels. Override only when a specific screen needs different emphasis.

leaves.label: Text background color
leaves.description: An optional fill drawn behind the subtitle text (a highlight pill). Off unless you set it; leave empty for plain text on the screen background.

leaves.label: Font family
leaves.description: The typeface of the subtitle.

leaves.label: Line height
leaves.description: Vertical spacing between lines of text — raise it to give multi-line text more breathing room.

leaves.label: Font size
leaves.description: Text size of the subtitle in pixels.

leaves.label: Font weight
leaves.description: How bold the text is, from Thin through Bold to Black.

leaves.label: Text color
leaves.description: The color of the subtitle text. Keep enough contrast with the background that it stays readable.

leaves.label: Text align
leaves.description: Horizontal alignment of the text: start (left), center, or end (right).

leaves.label: Strikethrough color
leaves.description: Color of a line-through decoration when the text is struck out (for example, an old price).

leaves.label: Background opacity
leaves.description: How see-through the text background fill is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid). Only matters when a background color is set.

leaves.label: Background radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding (px) of the text background fill; higher is softer.

fields.label: Space around the subtitle
fields.description: Adds empty space on each side of the subtitle, controlling the gap above it (to the title) and below it (to what follows). Leave it at the theme default unless the subtitle feels crowded. Increase the top value to separate it from the title, or reduce spacing to tighten the whole headline group.

fields.label: The featured image up top
fields.description: The hero is the large featured image at the top of a headline or wheel-picker screen, the picture that sells the screen at a glance. Turn it on, then upload a file or paste an image URL. Pick a high-quality, on-message visual (product, result, or lifestyle shot); on a paid landing page it is often the first thing a visitor sees. Sizing and position are set just below.

fields.label: The hero image itself
fields.description: Pick the actual hero image: upload a file from your computer or paste a direct image URL, then check the preview thumbnail. Use a high-resolution JPG or PNG so it stays crisp on large screens — uploads are optimized automatically for fast loading. To change it later, just upload or paste a new source here.

fields.label: How the image fills its box
fields.description: Sets how your image fits its box: Aspect Fit shows the whole image with no cropping (you may see empty bars at the sides), Aspect Fill crops the edges so it fully covers the box, Scale to Fill stretches it (can look distorted, avoid for photos), and Tile repeats it as a pattern. Default is Aspect Fit, which never distorts; switch to Aspect Fill when you want it edge-to-edge and don't mind some cropping.

fields.label: Fixed image width
fields.description: Optionally pin the hero image to a set width with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty in most cases — the image then sizes to the screen and stays responsive across devices, which almost always looks best on a landing page. Set a fixed width only when you need the image smaller than full-width or aligned to a specific size.

fields.label: Fixed image height
fields.description: Optionally pin the hero image to a set height with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty to let the image keep its natural proportions from the width — best for most screens. Use a fixed height when you want a consistent banner size; to size by screen proportion instead, use 'Image height relative to container' below, which takes priority over this value.

fields.label: Size the image by screen
fields.description: Sizes the hero image as a percentage of the screen height (0 to 100%), so it scales with the device, the more responsive way to size a hero. If set, it overrides any fixed height above. A common starting point is 30 to 50% for a prominent banner that still leaves room for your title and button below; leave it empty to size by proportions instead.

fields.label: How rounded the image is
fields.description: Rounds all four corners of the hero image; 0 is sharp and higher values (up to 50) make them softer and more rounded. The default is 0. A small radius around 8 to 16 gives a modern, friendly look; match it to the rounding used elsewhere in your funnel, like buttons and cards, so the page feels consistent.

fields.label: Space around the image
fields.description: Adds empty space on each side of the hero image (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't flush against the screen edges or crammed next to the title. Leave it at the theme default in most cases. Increase a side when the image feels too tight against nearby content, or reduce it for a full-bleed, edge-to-edge look.

fields.label: Where the image sits
fields.description: On headline screens, this sets where the hero image sits relative to your title and subtitle — above the text, below it, or beside it. Lead with your strongest element: image-on-top when the visual is the hook, text-on-top when the headline does the selling. The preview updates instantly, so try a couple and keep whichever reads clearest.

help-block-action-bar.title: Action Bar
help-block-action-bar.summary: The bottom button bar — your primary call-to-action and an optional secondary button.

fields.label: Main button label
fields.description: The text on your main call-to-action button — the one that moves visitors to the next screen. Make it a short, specific verb phrase tied to the action (Continue, Get my plan, Subscribe) rather than a generic word; clear, benefit-led labels lift click-through on a paid landing page. This text can be translated per language.

fields.label: Main button text style
fields.description: Typography for the main button label — font, weight, size, color, and alignment. Leave it on the theme defaults for a consistent look; bump the weight or size, or switch color, only when the label is hard to read against the button fill. Applies to the label in every language.

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: Fill drawn behind the label text (a highlight pill).

leaves.label: Font family
leaves.description: Typeface of the button label.

leaves.label: Line height
leaves.description: Vertical spacing of the label text.

leaves.label: Font size
leaves.description: Text size (px) of the label.

leaves.label: Font weight
leaves.description: How bold the label is.

leaves.label: Text color
leaves.description: Color of the label text.

leaves.label: Text align
leaves.description: Alignment of the label within the button.

leaves.label: Strikethrough color
leaves.description: Color of a line-through decoration when used (for example, an old price).

leaves.label: Background opacity
leaves.description: Transparency of the label background (0–100%).

leaves.label: Background radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding of the label background.

fields.label: Main button shape and fill
fields.description: Sets the main button's look — background color, border, corner radius, height, inner padding, and a full-width toggle. For an ad landing page keep it full-width and high-contrast so it reads as the obvious next step. The Visibility toggle hides the button entirely; only hide it when the screen forces a choice first, and never hide both buttons.

leaves.label: Visibility
leaves.description: Show or hide this button entirely. Never hide both buttons, or the screen has no way forward.

leaves.label: Full width
leaves.description: Stretch the button across the whole bar. Full-width reads as the obvious next step on a phone; turn it off for a button only as wide as its label.

leaves.label: Button height
leaves.description: Fixed height of the button in pixels. Keep it tap-friendly (≈44px or taller).

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: The button fill color.

leaves.label: Border width
leaves.description: Thickness (px) of the button outline; 0 hides it.

leaves.label: Border color
leaves.description: Color of that outline.

leaves.label: Corner radius
leaves.description: How rounded the button corners are (px); higher is softer.

leaves.label: Width
leaves.description: Explicit button width — used when Full width is off.

leaves.label: Button padding
leaves.description: Inner spacing between the label/icon and the button edges (top, right, bottom, left).

fields.label: Gradient on the main button
fields.description: An optional color gradient layered over the button's solid fill — set start and end colors, the angle, extra color stops, and an optional moving shimmer. Leave it off for a clean flat look; turn it on to make the call-to-action pop against a busy background. Keep enough contrast that the label stays easy to read.

leaves.label: Enable gradient
leaves.description: Off by default — the button uses a single flat color. Turn this on to blend colors across the fill for a richer look; turn it off for a clean solid button.

leaves.label: Detail level
leaves.description: A complexity switch (not saved on its own): Simple = just a start and end color; Medium = adds a direction angle and a shimmer toggle; Advanced = multi-stop colors plus a numeric angle, size and the full shimmer controls. Pick the depth you need.

leaves.label: Start color
leaves.description: The color the gradient begins with (the first color stop / left-most stop in Advanced).

leaves.label: End color
leaves.description: The color the gradient fades to (the last color stop). Keep enough contrast with the start color that the label stays readable.

leaves.label: Angle / direction
leaves.description: Which way the colors flow across the button. Medium offers preset directions (e.g. 90° left→right, 180° top→bottom); Advanced lets you type any angle from 0–360°.

leaves.label: Color stops (Advanced)
leaves.description: The full list of colors in the gradient. Add up to five stops and set each stop’s color and its position (0–100%) along the sweep, for multi-color blends beyond a simple two-color fade.

leaves.label: Gradient size (Advanced)
leaves.description: How far the gradient is stretched, from 50% (tight, punchy transition) to 200% (soft, gradual spread).

leaves.label: Shimmer
leaves.description: An optional animated sheen that sweeps across the button. When on you can tune the trigger (on hover, on a timer, or off), the streak color, its width and skew (slant), the duration of one sweep, and — for the timer trigger — the cycle gap between sweeps.

fields.label: Shadow under the main button
fields.description: An optional drop shadow beneath the button, with control over its color, blur, and vertical drop. A soft shadow lifts the call-to-action off the page so it feels tappable; keep it subtle (low blur, small offset) so it looks intentional rather than heavy. Leave it off if your theme is flat.

leaves.label: Enable shadow
leaves.description: Off by default. Turn on to cast a soft drop shadow beneath the button so it lifts off the background; off keeps it flat.

leaves.label: Color
leaves.description: The shadow color, including its transparency (default is a semi-transparent black). A tinted, low-opacity color gives a subtle lift.

leaves.label: Blur
leaves.description: How soft and spread-out the shadow is, from 0 (hard edge) to 50 (very diffuse).

leaves.label: Vertical offset
leaves.description: How far the shadow sits below (positive) or above (negative) the button, −50 to 50 px.

fields.label: Motion on the main button
fields.description: Optional animation for the call-to-action — pulse, glow, bounce, scale, fade-in, slide-up and more, plus an opacity control. A gentle pulse or glow can draw the eye and lift taps; save attention-grabbing effects for your key conversion screen and avoid stacking several. Leave it off for a calm, professional feel.

leaves.label: Enable effects
leaves.description: Off by default (gated on opacity). Turning it on sets the button to full opacity and a default Shimmer animation, then reveals the opacity slider and animation menu. (The animation choice is remembered but inactive while effects are off.)

leaves.label: Opacity
leaves.description: How see-through the whole button is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid).

leaves.label: Animation
leaves.description: An optional looping motion to draw the eye to the action — choose from None, Pulse, Shimmer, Bounce, Shake, Glow, Ripple, Scale, Fade In, Slide Up or Wiggle.

fields.label: Icon on the main button
fields.description: An optional icon next to the label — choose start or end placement, size, corner radius, and spacing, and how it fits its box (fit shows the whole icon, fill crops to cover). A small leading arrow or lock icon can reinforce the action; keep it in the same color family as the label. Leave it empty for a clean text-only button.

leaves.label: Enable icon
leaves.description: Off by default. Turn on to show an image (icon) alongside the button label; off for a text-only button.

leaves.label: Icon image
leaves.description: Upload an image file or paste an image URL — the icon shown next to the label. Leave empty to show no graphic.

leaves.label: Placement
leaves.description: Where the icon sits relative to the label: Start (before the text) or End (after it); the Fixed Start/End variants pin it to the button’s left/right edge; Top and Bottom stack it above or below the label.

leaves.label: Scale mode
leaves.description: How the image fits its box: Scale to Fill (stretch), Aspect Fit (show the whole icon, may letterbox), Aspect Fill (cover the box, may crop), or Center (no resize).

leaves.label: Width
leaves.description: The icon’s width in pixels (0–200).

leaves.label: Height
leaves.description: The icon’s height in pixels (0–200).

leaves.label: Corner radius
leaves.description: Rounding of the icon’s corners in pixels; raise it to clip a square image into a rounded or circular badge.

leaves.label: Icon padding
leaves.description: The space around the icon (top, right, bottom, left) — the gap between the icon and the label and the button edges.

fields.label: Secondary button label
fields.description: Text for the optional second button — use it for a side path like Skip, Maybe later, or Restore purchase, never your main goal. On funnel steps an easy escape route can cost conversions, so leave it empty unless you genuinely need the alternative; on a paywall a low-key secondary is fine.

fields.label: Secondary button text style
fields.description: Typography for the secondary button label — font, weight, size, color, and alignment. Style it deliberately quieter than the main button (lighter weight, muted color) so your primary call-to-action stays the obvious choice. Leave it on theme defaults unless the hierarchy looks off.

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: Fill drawn behind the label text (a highlight pill).

leaves.label: Font family
leaves.description: Typeface of the button label.

leaves.label: Line height
leaves.description: Vertical spacing of the label text.

leaves.label: Font size
leaves.description: Text size (px) of the label.

leaves.label: Font weight
leaves.description: How bold the label is.

leaves.label: Text color
leaves.description: Color of the label text.

leaves.label: Text align
leaves.description: Alignment of the label within the button.

leaves.label: Strikethrough color
leaves.description: Color of a line-through decoration when used (for example, an old price).

leaves.label: Background opacity
leaves.description: Transparency of the label background (0–100%).

leaves.label: Background radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding of the label background.

fields.label: Secondary button shape and fill
fields.description: Sets the secondary button's look — background, border, corner radius, height, padding, and a full-width toggle. Give it lower visual weight than the main button (an outline or transparent fill works well) so it doesn't compete with your call-to-action. The Visibility toggle hides it; never hide both the primary and secondary buttons.

leaves.label: Visibility
leaves.description: Show or hide this button entirely. Never hide both buttons, or the screen has no way forward.

leaves.label: Full width
leaves.description: Stretch the button across the whole bar. Full-width reads as the obvious next step on a phone; turn it off for a button only as wide as its label.

leaves.label: Button height
leaves.description: Fixed height of the button in pixels. Keep it tap-friendly (≈44px or taller).

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: The button fill color.

leaves.label: Border width
leaves.description: Thickness (px) of the button outline; 0 hides it.

leaves.label: Border color
leaves.description: Color of that outline.

leaves.label: Corner radius
leaves.description: How rounded the button corners are (px); higher is softer.

leaves.label: Width
leaves.description: Explicit button width — used when Full width is off.

leaves.label: Button padding
leaves.description: Inner spacing between the label/icon and the button edges (top, right, bottom, left).

fields.label: Gradient on the secondary button
fields.description: An optional color gradient over the secondary button's solid fill (start/end colors, angle, stops, optional shimmer). Usually leave this off — a gradient draws attention, which you want on your main call-to-action, not the side path. Turn it on only if a flat secondary clashes with your theme.

leaves.label: Enable gradient
leaves.description: Off by default — the button uses a single flat color. Turn this on to blend colors across the fill for a richer look; turn it off for a clean solid button.

leaves.label: Detail level
leaves.description: A complexity switch (not saved on its own): Simple = just a start and end color; Medium = adds a direction angle and a shimmer toggle; Advanced = multi-stop colors plus a numeric angle, size and the full shimmer controls. Pick the depth you need.

leaves.label: Start color
leaves.description: The color the gradient begins with (the first color stop / left-most stop in Advanced).

leaves.label: End color
leaves.description: The color the gradient fades to (the last color stop). Keep enough contrast with the start color that the label stays readable.

leaves.label: Angle / direction
leaves.description: Which way the colors flow across the button. Medium offers preset directions (e.g. 90° left→right, 180° top→bottom); Advanced lets you type any angle from 0–360°.

leaves.label: Color stops (Advanced)
leaves.description: The full list of colors in the gradient. Add up to five stops and set each stop’s color and its position (0–100%) along the sweep, for multi-color blends beyond a simple two-color fade.

leaves.label: Gradient size (Advanced)
leaves.description: How far the gradient is stretched, from 50% (tight, punchy transition) to 200% (soft, gradual spread).

leaves.label: Shimmer
leaves.description: An optional animated sheen that sweeps across the button. When on you can tune the trigger (on hover, on a timer, or off), the streak color, its width and skew (slant), the duration of one sweep, and — for the timer trigger — the cycle gap between sweeps.

fields.label: Shadow under the secondary button
fields.description: An optional drop shadow under the secondary button (color, blur, vertical drop). Keep it lighter than the main button's shadow, or off entirely, so the secondary stays visually subordinate to your call-to-action.

leaves.label: Enable shadow
leaves.description: Off by default. Turn on to cast a soft drop shadow beneath the button so it lifts off the background; off keeps it flat.

leaves.label: Color
leaves.description: The shadow color, including its transparency (default is a semi-transparent black). A tinted, low-opacity color gives a subtle lift.

leaves.label: Blur
leaves.description: How soft and spread-out the shadow is, from 0 (hard edge) to 50 (very diffuse).

leaves.label: Vertical offset
leaves.description: How far the shadow sits below (positive) or above (negative) the button, −50 to 50 px.

fields.label: Motion on the secondary button
fields.description: Adds optional movement to the secondary (lower-priority) button, such as pulse, glow, or bounce, plus an opacity control to fade it. Leave this off by default. Animation draws the eye, so reserve it for your main button only; making the alternative path move competes with your primary call to action and typically lowers conversions.

leaves.label: Enable effects
leaves.description: Off by default (gated on opacity). Turning it on sets the button to full opacity and a default Shimmer animation, then reveals the opacity slider and animation menu. (The animation choice is remembered but inactive while effects are off.)

leaves.label: Opacity
leaves.description: How see-through the whole button is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid).

leaves.label: Animation
leaves.description: An optional looping motion to draw the eye to the action — choose from None, Pulse, Shimmer, Bounce, Shake, Glow, Ripple, Scale, Fade In, Slide Up or Wiggle.

fields.label: Icon on the secondary button
fields.description: An optional icon on the secondary button — placement (start or end), size, corner radius, spacing, and how it fits its box (fit shows the whole icon, fill crops to cover). Usually leave it empty so the secondary stays understated; add one only when it clarifies the action, like a back arrow for Go back.

leaves.label: Enable icon
leaves.description: Off by default. Turn on to show an image (icon) alongside the button label; off for a text-only button.

leaves.label: Icon image
leaves.description: Upload an image file or paste an image URL — the icon shown next to the label. Leave empty to show no graphic.

leaves.label: Placement
leaves.description: Where the icon sits relative to the label: Start (before the text) or End (after it); the Fixed Start/End variants pin it to the button’s left/right edge; Top and Bottom stack it above or below the label.

leaves.label: Scale mode
leaves.description: How the image fits its box: Scale to Fill (stretch), Aspect Fit (show the whole icon, may letterbox), Aspect Fill (cover the box, may crop), or Center (no resize).

leaves.label: Width
leaves.description: The icon’s width in pixels (0–200).

leaves.label: Height
leaves.description: The icon’s height in pixels (0–200).

leaves.label: Corner radius
leaves.description: Rounding of the icon’s corners in pixels; raise it to clip a square image into a rounded or circular badge.

leaves.label: Icon padding
leaves.description: The space around the icon (top, right, bottom, left) — the gap between the icon and the label and the button edges.

help-block-background.title: Background
help-block-background.summary: What fills the whole screen behind your content: a solid color, a photo, or a looping video.

fields.label: What Fills The Background
fields.description: Chooses what sits behind your content: a solid color, a photo, or a video clip, and reveals the matching control below. Defaults to a solid color. Use solid for clean question screens, a photo for emotive intro screens, and video only for short high-impact openers, since heavy video slows loading and can lose paid-ad visitors.

fields.label: Solid Background Fill
fields.description: Sets the single color behind the whole screen when the background is a solid color. Defaults to white. Match it to your theme and ad creative, and keep it high-contrast against your text and buttons so everything stays easy to read on a phone.

fields.label: Full-Screen Background Photo
fields.description: Uploads an image that fills the screen background when the background is set to Photo. It scales to cover the whole screen, so edges can get cropped on different phone sizes, keep your focal point centered. If you put text on top, choose a darker or dimmed image so your copy stays readable.

fields.label: Full-Screen Background Video
fields.description: Uploads a short clip that fills the screen background when the background is set to Video Clip; it loops on its own. Keep it brief and lightweight, large videos slow the first load and can lose paid-ad visitors before they engage. Make sure any text over it stays readable across the looping frames.

fields.label: Tint The Phone's Top Bar
fields.description: Sets the color of the surrounding system bars on web funnels, the strip at the top showing time and battery, and the bottom address bar. Leave it unset for almost every screen so it inherits your onboarding default. Set a color only when you want the phone's frame to blend into a full-bleed background for a seamless look.

help-block-basic-config.title: Basic Config
help-block-basic-config.summary: Screen-level behaviour: entrance animations, cached media, a device-permission prompt, and auto-advance.

fields.label: Play Screen Animations
fields.description: Turns on the entrance, exit, and element animations you set up in the screen's animation settings; when off, the screen simply appears instantly. Use it on intro and hero screens where motion feels polished and guides the eye. Leave it off on dense question screens where visitors want the controls ready to tap right away.

fields.label: Reuse cached media
fields.description: When on, the screen reuses media it has already cached instead of re-downloading it, which can speed up loading for visitors on slow or flaky connections. Leave it off by default for standard web ad funnels, since there's nothing to reuse until assets are cached. Turn it on only if you ship pre-bundled assets or expect a lot of poor-connectivity traffic.

fields.label: Ask For A Device Permission
fields.description: When on, this screen pops the phone's own permission request, notifications, location, or ad tracking, chosen in the field below, as it appears. This fires in the native app SDK, not on a plain web page. Put it on a screen that first explains why you need it so far more people tap Allow.

fields.label: Which Permission To Ask For
fields.description: Picks which device permission this screen requests: push notifications, ad tracking (needed for accurate ad attribution on iPhones), or location. Only shows when the permission request is turned on. Choose what your funnel truly needs, ad tracking if you rely on ad-network attribution, notifications for re-engaging users later.

fields.label: Auto-Advance After A Delay
fields.description: When on, the screen moves to the next step on its own after the countdown you set below, with a visible timer. Off by default. Great for splash or 'analyzing...' screens, but never use it where visitors must tap or answer, like questions or your paywall, or you'll skip them past the response or sale.

fields.label: Auto-Advance Duration
fields.description: The number of seconds or minutes (unit chosen below) before the screen moves on by itself, from 1 to 300. Only used when auto-advance is on. Keep it short, about 2 to 4 seconds for a splash or 'analyzing...' screen, so visitors aren't left waiting and bouncing.

fields.label: Seconds Or Minutes
fields.description: Sets whether the auto-advance duration above counts in seconds or minutes. Only shows when auto-advance is on. Seconds is the right choice for nearly every onboarding screen; minutes is rarely useful and risks visitors leaving before the screen ever advances.

help-block-carousel.title: Carousel
help-block-carousel.summary: An auto-advancing slide deck — the slide template, total play time, each slide’s text and picture and timing, and the per-slide text/image styles.

fields.label: Slide content template
fields.description: Sets which layers each slide shows: Image Only is just the picture, Image + Title adds one headline, Image + Title + Subtitle adds a supporting line, and Image + Title + 2 Subtitles shows all four text layers. Choosing a richer template reveals its matching text and style fields below. Default to Image + Title for clean, fast-reading slides and add subtitles only when each slide genuinely needs more copy.

fields.label: Total play time
fields.description: The total time in seconds for the whole carousel to play through once before it stops or the visitor moves on (0.1–120s). This total is split across slides by each slide's timing slider, so changing it speeds up or slows every slide proportionally. Start around 3–5 seconds per slide (about 12–20s for four slides) — long enough to read each line, short enough to keep momentum and avoid stalling the visitor.

fields.label: Slide headline
fields.description: The main headline on this slide, shown only when the slide template includes a title. Keep it short and benefit-led so it lands in the few seconds the slide is on screen. You can drop in the visitor's earlier answers with @variable, plus countdown timers and styled label chips; if your funnel runs in several languages, you edit this text per language.

fields.label: Slide supporting line
fields.description: The line under the headline, shown only when the slide template is Image + Title + Subtitle or richer. Use it to back up the headline with a quick proof point or detail rather than repeat it. It supports @variable personalization, countdown timers, and styled chips, is edited per language, and only appears after you set a slide template that includes a subtitle.

fields.label: Slide extra line
fields.description: A third text line below the supporting line, available only with the Image + Title + 2 Subtitles template. Use it sparingly for one last small detail like a disclaimer or extra proof, since four text layers over an image quickly overcrowd a slide and slow reading. Supports @variable personalization, countdown timers, and styled chips, and is edited per language.

fields.label: Slide picture
fields.description: The image shown on this slide, required on every slide no matter which template you pick. Drag-and-drop or click to upload, and Segmently serves a fast-loading optimized version automatically. Use a high-quality picture that matches the slide's message; how it fills the slide is set in Image styles below, and a slide left without an image shows blank, so set one on every slide before publishing.

fields.label: How long this slide shows
fields.description: A two-thumb slider that sets the window, as a share of the carousel's total duration, during which this slide is on screen. Drag the thumbs apart to give this slide a longer share, which leaves less time for the others. For example, a 25% window at a 20-second total keeps this slide visible about 5 seconds; keep slides spread evenly and only widen the most persuasive one.

fields.label: Title look and spacing
fields.description: Open this to override how the carousel's headline looks: font size, weight, color, alignment, and the padding around the text. It only shows when the template includes a title. Leave it untouched to inherit your theme so screens stay consistent; change it only when one carousel needs a bigger or bolder headline, and note the overrides apply to the title on every slide.

leaves.label: Font size
leaves.description: Text size (px) of the slide headline.

leaves.label: Font weight
leaves.description: How bold the headline is.

leaves.label: Text color
leaves.description: Headline color.

leaves.label: Text align
leaves.description: Left, center, or right alignment of the headline.

leaves.label: Line height
leaves.description: Vertical spacing between headline lines.

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: Fill drawn behind the headline text.

leaves.label: Background opacity
leaves.description: Transparency of that headline background (0–100%).

leaves.label: Background radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding of the headline background.

leaves.label: Headline padding
leaves.description: Space around the headline text (top, right, bottom, left). All these overrides apply to the headline on every slide.

fields.label: Supporting line look
fields.description: Open this to override the supporting line's font size, weight, color, alignment, and the padding around it; it shows only when the template includes a subtitle. Keep this line visually lighter than the headline (smaller or thinner) so the slide reads in the right order. Leave it on theme defaults for consistency unless this carousel needs a custom look, and remember changes apply to every slide.

leaves.label: Font size
leaves.description: Text size (px) of the slide supporting line.

leaves.label: Font weight
leaves.description: How bold the supporting line is.

leaves.label: Text color
leaves.description: Supporting line color.

leaves.label: Text align
leaves.description: Left, center, or right alignment of the supporting line.

leaves.label: Line height
leaves.description: Vertical spacing between supporting line lines.

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: Fill drawn behind the supporting line text.

leaves.label: Background opacity
leaves.description: Transparency of that supporting line background (0–100%).

leaves.label: Background radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding of the supporting line background.

leaves.label: Supporting line padding
leaves.description: Space around the supporting line text (top, right, bottom, left). All these overrides apply to the supporting line on every slide.

fields.label: Extra line look
fields.description: Open this to override the third line's font size, weight, color, alignment, and the padding around it; it appears only with the Image + Title + 2 Subtitles template. Style it as the smallest, quietest text so it never competes with the headline or supporting line. Leave it on theme defaults unless you truly need a change, since overrides apply to this line on every slide of the carousel.

leaves.label: Font size
leaves.description: Text size (px) of the slide extra line.

leaves.label: Font weight
leaves.description: How bold the extra line is.

leaves.label: Text color
leaves.description: Extra line color.

leaves.label: Text align
leaves.description: Left, center, or right alignment of the extra line.

leaves.label: Line height
leaves.description: Vertical spacing between extra line lines.

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: Fill drawn behind the extra line text.

leaves.label: Background opacity
leaves.description: Transparency of that extra line background (0–100%).

leaves.label: Background radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding of the extra line background.

leaves.label: Extra line padding
leaves.description: Space around the extra line text (top, right, bottom, left). All these overrides apply to the extra line on every slide.

fields.label: Image size and fit
fields.description: Open this to control the slide image's width, height, corner radius, and how it fills its box: Fit shows the whole image (may leave bands), Fill covers the box (edges may crop), Crop trims to the exact box, and Tile repeats it. You also set the padding around the image. Fill is the usual choice for full-bleed slides and Fit keeps the whole graphic visible; settings apply to the image on every slide.

leaves.label: Image width
leaves.description: Width (px) of the slide's picture.

leaves.label: Image height
leaves.description: Height (px) of the slide's picture.

leaves.label: Scale mode
leaves.description: How the picture fills its box: Fit shows the whole image, Fill covers the box (edges may crop), Crop trims to the box, Tile repeats it.

leaves.label: Corner radius
leaves.description: How rounded the picture corners are (px).

leaves.label: Image padding
leaves.description: Space around the picture inside the slide. These overrides apply to the picture on every slide.

fields.label: Image box height and position
fields.description: Controls the box that holds each slide's image, separate from the image's own styling. Set how tall the box is (Auto fits the image, Fixed is an exact pixel height, Percent is a share of the slide), where the image sits inside it, and the padding around it. Leave it on Auto unless you want every slide's image to occupy the same vertical space so slides don't jump in size as visitors swipe.

leaves.label: Vertical align
leaves.description: Where the image sits within its box — top, center, or bottom.

leaves.label: Height mode
leaves.description: How the image box is sized: Auto fits the content, Fixed is an exact pixel height, Percent is a share of the slide.

leaves.label: Height value
leaves.description: The height number used by the chosen mode (px or %).

leaves.label: Container padding
leaves.description: Empty space inside the image box (top, right, bottom, left).

fields.label: Text box height and position
fields.description: Controls the box that holds all of a slide's text (title, subtitle, detail) as a group, separate from styling each line. Set how tall the box is (Auto fits the text, Fixed is exact pixels, Percent is a share of the slide), where the text block sits, and the padding around it. Leave it on Auto unless you want text anchored the same way on every slide, for example always sitting in the lower third over the image.

leaves.label: Vertical align
leaves.description: Where the text block sits within its box — top, center, or bottom.

leaves.label: Height mode
leaves.description: How the text block box is sized: Auto fits the content, Fixed is an exact pixel height, Percent is a share of the slide.

leaves.label: Height value
leaves.description: The height number used by the chosen mode (px or %).

leaves.label: Container padding
leaves.description: Empty space inside the text block box (top, right, bottom, left).

help-block-media.title: Media
help-block-media.summary: The screen's image or video block — its source, size, placement, rounding, and an optional fade overlay.

fields.label: Show an image or video
fields.description: Turns the image or video block on or off for this screen; off means no visual is shown. Turn it on to add a supporting visual, since on a paid landing page a relevant image or video builds trust and lifts conversion. When enabled, it starts with sensible styling from your design theme that you can fine-tune in the fields below.

fields.label: Image or video
fields.description: Pick whether this screen shows an image or a video. Use an image for a fast, lightweight visual that loads instantly; use a video for short product demos or motion that holds attention (it can loop). Switching type clears the current media, so choose before you upload. Keep videos short and light so the page stays fast, since slow loads cost conversions on paid traffic.

fields.label: The image for this screen
fields.description: Add this screen's image by uploading a file from your computer or pasting a direct image URL, then confirm it in the preview. Use a high-quality JPG or PNG that's on-message for the screen — uploads are optimized automatically for fast loading on every device. To replace it later, upload or paste a new source here.

fields.label: The video for this screen
fields.description: Add a video by uploading a file or pasting a direct video URL. Keep it short (a few seconds, ideally under ~30s) and lightweight so the page loads fast — long or heavy videos hurt conversion on paid traffic. Uploads are converted automatically to play reliably across devices, and you can pair this with the loop option below to replay it continuously.

fields.label: Where the media starts on top
fields.description: Sets where the media begins from the top of the screen. Screen Top runs it edge-to-edge to the very top (great for a full-bleed hero), Navigation Bar starts it just below the header, and Safe Area keeps it clear of phone notches and rounded corners. Pick Screen Top for an immersive banner, Safe Area when nothing should ever be clipped. This is locked if you set a media height percentage below, which positions it for you.

fields.label: How media fills its box
fields.description: Controls how the media fills its box. Aspect Fit shows the whole thing without cropping (you may see empty bars), Aspect Fill covers the box completely but may crop edges, and Scale to Fill stretches it, which distorts photos, so avoid that. The positional options (Top, Bottom, Center, and so on) crop to fill while keeping that part in view. Aspect Fill is the usual pick for an edge-to-edge banner; use Aspect Fit when nothing should be cropped.

fields.label: How tall the media is
fields.description: Sets the media height as a share of the screen (0 to 100%), so it scales on every device; the default is 50%. Use a larger percentage for an immersive, image-led screen and a smaller one when you need room for the title, text, or button below; on a choice screen, keep it modest so the options stay visible without scrolling. Setting a value pins the media just below the header for a consistent layout.

fields.label: How rounded the media is
fields.description: Rounds the corners of the media block; 0 is sharp and higher values (up to 50) make them softer. A small radius around 8 to 16 gives a modern, polished look; match it to the rounding on your buttons and cards so the whole screen feels consistent. Leave it at 0 for full-bleed media that touches the screen edges.

fields.label: Replay the video on a loop
fields.description: When on, the video replays continuously; when off, it plays once and stops on the last frame. Only applies to video media. Turn looping on for short ambient background clips that hold attention; turn it off for a demo or explainer you want watched once, so it doesn't loop distractingly while the visitor reads.

fields.label: Space around the media
fields.description: Adds empty space on the four sides of the media (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't flush against the screen edges or neighboring content. Leave it at the default for a full-width visual. Increase a side to inset the media and give it a framed look with breathing room, rather than edge-to-edge.

fields.label: Fade over the media
fields.description: Lays a soft, see-through fade (usually dark) over the media so any text or button on top stays readable against a busy image. Turn it on whenever you place a title, subtitle, or button over the media; without it, light areas of the image can wash out your copy. When enabled, you get controls below to set the fade's height and color.

fields.label: How far the fade extends
fields.description: Controls how far the fade reaches across the media (0 to 100%). Match it to where your text or button sits: if the copy is near the bottom, a 30 to 50% fade from that edge usually gives enough contrast without darkening the whole image. Increase it if text is still hard to read, decrease it to show more of the image clearly.

fields.label: Color of the fade
fields.description: Picks the color of the fade over the media. Use a dark color (usually black) behind light or white text, or a light color behind dark text; the fade goes from this color to fully transparent so the image still shows through. Match it to your background or brand color for a seamless look, and choose whichever direction gives your copy the strongest contrast.

help-content-text.title: Content
help-content-text.summary: The headline, subtitle, and optional hero image — the words and lead visual that carry the screen.

fields.label: Your main headline
fields.description: The title is the biggest, first thing a visitor reads, so it carries most of the weight on whether they keep going. Turn it on, then write one short benefit-led line, like an ad headline rather than a sentence. Type @ to drop in an earlier answer (for example @user_goal) so it feels personal, and style it under the gear icon below.

fields.label: Write the headline text
fields.description: This is where you type the actual headline; keep it short and benefit-driven. Type @ to pull in a visitor's earlier answer (such as @user_goal) for personalization, add a link inside the text with @link, or insert a countdown with @countdown to create urgency on offer screens. If your funnel runs in more than one language, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

fields.label: Title look and emphasis
fields.description: Override how the headline looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and an optional highlight behind the text. By default it inherits your project theme, which keeps every screen consistent, so most funnels never need to touch this. Override only when one screen needs extra punch, like a bigger color headline on your hero.

leaves.label: Text background color
leaves.description: An optional fill drawn behind the title text (a highlight pill). Off unless you set it; leave empty for plain text on the screen background.

leaves.label: Font family
leaves.description: The typeface of the title.

leaves.label: Line height
leaves.description: Vertical spacing between lines of text — raise it to give multi-line text more breathing room.

leaves.label: Font size
leaves.description: Text size of the title in pixels.

leaves.label: Font weight
leaves.description: How bold the text is, from Thin through Bold to Black.

leaves.label: Text color
leaves.description: The color of the title text. Keep enough contrast with the background that it stays readable.

leaves.label: Text align
leaves.description: Horizontal alignment of the text: start (left), center, or end (right).

leaves.label: Strikethrough color
leaves.description: Color of a line-through decoration when the text is struck out (for example, an old price).

leaves.label: Background opacity
leaves.description: How see-through the text background fill is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid). Only matters when a background color is set.

leaves.label: Background radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding (px) of the text background fill; higher is softer.

fields.label: Space around the title
fields.description: Adds empty space on each side of the title (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't cramped against the screen edges or the text below. Leave it at the theme default unless the title feels too tight or too far from the next element. Increase a side to give it room, or decrease to pull elements closer together.

fields.label: The line under your title
fields.description: The subtitle is the supporting line beneath your title; use it to expand the promise, add proof, or hint at what happens next. Turn it on and keep it to one short sentence; it shows smaller and lighter than the title by default so the headline stays dominant. Like the title, you can personalize it with @ variables. Skip it on screens where the title already says everything.

fields.label: Write the subtitle text
fields.description: Type the supporting line that sits under your title here, one short sentence that reinforces the offer or tells the visitor what comes next. The same shortcuts work as in the title: type @ to insert an earlier answer, @link to add a clickable link, or @countdown for urgency. If your funnel is multilingual, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

fields.label: Subtitle look and emphasis
fields.description: Change how the subtitle looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and an optional background — styled separately from the title so you can tune each one. fields.label: Choose where the answer is saved

Reuse an existing variable when this screen asks about the same thing as another screen (so all answers feed one value), and create a new one for a brand-new question. This is the key step: nothing downstream (branching, analytics, paywall personalization) works until a variable is chosen here.

fields.label: Name the new variable
fields.description: A readable name for the variable you're creating, like User Goal, that must be unique across the funnel. It becomes the reference you use elsewhere — usually a lowercased, underscored form such as @user_goal in dynamic text and conditions. Pick a clear name that describes the answer (User Goal, Experience Level) rather than the screen, since later references depend on it and you won't want to rename it.

fields.label: What kind of value it stores
fields.description: Sets the kind of value this variable holds, which must fit the screen. Use Choice for single-select screens, Multiple choices for multi-select lists or grids where visitors pick several, Number for numeric input like age or weight, and Text for free-form typed answers. The screen only offers compatible types, and the Choice options you can branch and report on are defined below.

fields.label: Internal note (optional)
fields.description: An optional internal note explaining what this variable is for. It only shows as a tooltip in the editor when you hover the variable later — visitors never see it and it has no effect on the funnel. A one-line note like "visitor's primary fitness goal" is worth adding so you and teammates remember the variable's purpose when reusing it across screens.

fields.label: List the stored answers
fields.description: For Choice and Multiple-choice variables, list the values this variable can store, such as lose_weight, build_muscle, or stay_fit; add, rename, or remove them here. These stored values are separate from the labels visitors see — you connect each one to a visible item in the Value Mapping table below. Keep one option per real answer so your routing and analytics stay clean.

fields.label: The stored value for this option
fields.description: This is the value saved to the variable and used in conditions and analytics, not the text visitors see (that lives on the list or grid item). Keep it stable and lowercase with underscores, like lose_weight. You can rename it, but that changes every place it's referenced, so avoid renaming after the funnel is published and collecting data.

fields.label: Link a choice to this value
fields.description: Connect this option to the on-screen choice (the list or grid row) that should set it, so when a visitor picks that row the variable stores this value. Each visible choice should map to one option so answers record correctly, and several options can point to the same row if needed. If a choice has no option mapped to it, the editor flags it as unmapped, so fix that before publishing or it won't record an answer.

fields.label: Add an option value
fields.description: Type a value for a new option on this variable and click Add; it joins the options list and the mapping table below. Use a stable, lowercase, underscore-style value such as maintain_weight so routing and analytics stay clean. After adding it, map it to the matching on-screen item below — otherwise a visitor choosing that answer won't store anything.

fields.label: Add points based on answers
fields.description: Optional and advanced: have each answer on this screen add points to a number variable, like a quiz or lead-qualification score. You can later branch on the total (high score to a premium paywall) or send it to analytics. Skip this unless you're scoring answers, since most screens don't need it.

fields.label: Which score this adds to
fields.description: Choose the number variable this answer adds points to, such as a quiz_score or lead_score total. Only Number-type variables appear here, so if the list is empty, create a number variable first. Use one shared score variable across all the screens you want to total up, with the points set in the score value field.

fields.label: Points this answer adds

Give higher-intent answers larger values and weaker ones smaller or zero, for example 'ready to buy' = 10 and 'just browsing' = 1. Keep a consistent scale across all answers so the final total is meaningful for branching or analytics.

fields.label: Rebuild options from the items

Warning: it replaces the existing options (a confirmation shows old versus new first), so custom options or mappings not present in the items can be lost. Avoid it when the variable is shared with other screens, and most funnels rarely need it once options are set.

help-options-grid-single.title: Options
help-options-grid-single.summary: The answer choices visitors pick from — selection mode, list-or-grid layout, item states, spacing, and styling.

fields.label: What each choice shows
fields.description: Pick which parts each choice displays — title only, image plus title, checkbox with title and subtitle, and so on; available combos depend on your selection mode and layout. Adding an element reveals its style controls and means you must supply that content (image or subtitle) on every item. Default to title (plus a checkbox for multi-select) and add an image only when it aids the choice.

fields.label: Shuffle item order
fields.description: When enabled, randomizes the order items appear to users on each view. Useful for A/B testing, survey randomization, and reducing position bias in multi-select scenarios.

fields.label: Cap on multi-select picks
fields.description: Limits how many items a visitor can choose on a multi-select screen. Set a small cap (e.g. 3) to keep answers focused and the next step manageable; leave it unlimited to let them pick freely. This control only appears on multi-select screens and is ignored everywhere else.

fields.label: Vertical alignment of items
fields.description: Aligns each choice's content to the top, center, or bottom of its cell. It's most noticeable in grid layouts where cells are taller than their content; center usually looks balanced. In simple lists it has little visible effect, so center is a safe default.

fields.label: Even grid cell heights
fields.description: On a grid, choose whether all cells stretch to the same maximum height for tidy, even rows, or each cell sizes to its own content (giving rows of varying height). Turn it on for a clean, consistent grid; turn it off when items have very different content lengths. Only applies to grid layouts.

fields.label: Unselected item look
fields.description: The default look of each choice before it's tapped — background, border, corner radius, and an optional gradient. Keep it neutral and calm so the selected state can stand out; the contrast between this and the selected look is what tells visitors their tap registered. Pair it with the Selected item look.

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: The fill behind an option the visitor has NOT selected.

leaves.label: Border width
leaves.description: Thickness (px) of the outline around an unselected option; 0 hides it.

leaves.label: Border color
leaves.description: Color of that outline.

leaves.label: Corner radius
leaves.description: How rounded the option corners are (px); higher is softer.

leaves.label: Gradient fill
leaves.description: Optional gradient that replaces the flat background color for a richer look.

fields.label: Selected item look
fields.description: How a choice looks once tapped — background, border, corner radius, and optional gradient. Make it clearly distinct from the unselected look (an accent border or filled background) so visitors get instant confirmation; weak feedback here causes hesitation and drop-off. Your theme's accent color is a reliable choice.

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: The highlight fill behind the option the visitor HAS picked.

leaves.label: Border width
leaves.description: Outline thickness for the selected option.

leaves.label: Border color
leaves.description: Outline color for the selected option — often your accent color.

leaves.label: Corner radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding for the selected option; usually matches the unselected state.

leaves.label: Gradient fill
leaves.description: Optional gradient highlight for the selected option.

fields.label: Padding inside each item
fields.description: The space between each item's edge and its content (title, image, checkbox), set per side — top, end, bottom, start. More padding makes items feel roomy and easier to tap; too little looks cramped. Around 12–16px on all sides reads well on mobile, and the setting applies to every item.

fields.label: Margin around the whole list
fields.description: The outer space between the screen edges and the first and last items, set per side (top, end, bottom, start). Use it to keep the list off the screen edges and aligned with your other sections. This is the outside spacing — for the gap inside each item use Padding inside each item instead.

fields.label: Gap between choices
fields.description: The spacing between adjacent choices — a vertical gap in lists, the gap between cells in grids. Around 8–12px keeps items clearly separate and easy to tap without wasting space. Increase it for a more airy feel, or decrease it to fit more options above the fold.

fields.label: Grid cell proportions
fields.description: Sets each grid cell's height as a percentage of its width: 100 is square, above 100 makes taller cells, below 100 makes wider, shorter cells. Pick taller cells for image-led options and square for balanced icon-and-text choices. Only appears on two-column grids — try 100 first, then adjust to fit your content.

fields.label: Image area in each card
fields.description: On grid cards that show an image, this sets the image region as a whole: where it sits in the card, how tall it is (a fixed height or sized to fit its content), and the spacing around it. By default it fits the content, but setting one fixed height keeps every card's image lined up at the same level, which looks more polished and trustworthy on an ad landing page. This shapes the image's container only; the image's own size and corners are set separately in the item image styles.

leaves.label: Vertical align
leaves.description: Where the image sits within its region — top, center, or bottom.

leaves.label: Content align
leaves.description: Horizontal alignment of the image inside the region.

leaves.label: Height mode
leaves.description: How the image region is sized: a fixed pixel height, a percent of the cell, or auto.

leaves.label: Height value
leaves.description: The height number used by the chosen mode (px or %).

leaves.label: Region padding
leaves.description: Empty space inside the image region around the image (top, right, bottom, left).

fields.label: Text area in each card
fields.description: On grid cards with an image, this sets the title-and-subtitle region as a block: where it sits in the card, how tall it is (a fixed height or sized to fit its content), and the spacing around it. It fits the content by default, but choosing one fixed height keeps the text blocks aligned across every card so the row reads as a clean, scannable set. This controls the text region's position only; the actual fonts and colors of the title and subtitle are set in their own style sections.

leaves.label: Vertical align
leaves.description: Where the title/subtitle block sits within its region.

leaves.label: Content align
leaves.description: Horizontal alignment of the text inside the region.

leaves.label: Height mode
leaves.description: Fixed px, percent of the cell, or auto height for the text region.

leaves.label: Height value

leaves.label: Region padding

fields.description: On grid cells, show or hide the selection checkbox and place it in a corner (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right) with an optional offset. Keep it visible on multi-select grids so visitors can see what they've picked; top-right is a common, unobtrusive spot. Only appears on grid layouts.

leaves.label: Position

help-block-stepper.title: Stepper
help-block-stepper.summary: An auto-advancing progress bar that steps through segments — the progress layout, total playback time, the bar’s colours / thickness / padding, the media-area split, and each step’s title / subtitle / description / image styles.

fields.label: Select progress stepper layout
fields.description: Determines the visual layout for progress steps. Circle displays steps as an orbital arrangement (no image container); Image Container First and Chart Container First show image/text in a container with progress bar. Defines which content elements are shown in each segment (image visibility, title, subtitle, description).

fields.label: How long the progress runs
fields.description: Total time, in seconds (1-120), for the progress sequence to advance through all its steps before the screen continues. Aim for about 4-8 seconds: long enough to feel like real work is happening for the user, short enough to avoid drop-off. Use the play/pause preview to test the pacing against your step text.

fields.label: Color of the empty track
fields.description: Color of the unfilled part of the progress bar — the portion not yet completed. Defaults to light gray (#E0E0E0), which works for most screens. Keep it clearly lighter than the fill color so the user can read their progress at a glance, or match your page background for a subtler look.

fields.label: Color of the completed portion
fields.description: Color of the filled part of the progress bar that grows as the sequence advances, signaling completion to the user. Defaults to green (#4CAF50). Use your brand accent or a clearly positive color, and keep strong contrast against the empty track so progress reads instantly.

fields.label: How thick the progress bar is
fields.description: Height of the filled bar in pixels (0-50, default 4px). 4-8px reads as a clean, modern bar; go thicker only for a bold, attention-grabbing indicator. Set it equal to or greater than the track thickness so the fill sits flush over the track instead of looking sunken.

fields.label: How thick the empty track is
fields.description: Height of the background track in pixels (0-50, default 4px). Keep it equal to the fill thickness for a standard flat bar — the safe choice for most screens. Make it larger than the fill only if you want a recessed groove look, since mismatched values change how the fill sits inside the track.

fields.label: Space around the progress bar
fields.description: Sets the empty space, in pixels, on each side of the progress bar: top, right, bottom, left. The default is usually 0 for a tight bar that sits close to your content; add top and bottom padding to give it room from the title or image above and below. On an ad funnel a progress bar with a little breathing room reads as a quick, low-effort flow, which keeps people moving forward.

fields.label: Split between media and progress
fields.description: Percentage of the screen's vertical space (0-100, default 50%) given to the image/text area; the rest goes to the progress area. Raise it above 50% when your image or step text needs more room, or lower it to make the progress bar more prominent. This appears only for the Image First or Chart First layouts and is hidden for the orbital Circle layout.

A clear, uncrowded title is the first thing visitors read, so the small spacing tweak helps them grasp the offer fast and stay in the funnel.

The default is usually 0; add top padding to set the subtitle off from the title above and bottom padding to separate it from the description below. Adjust it only when the subtitle feels cramped against neighboring text, so the supporting line stays easy to scan and reinforces your pitch.

fields.description: Text styling for segment descriptions including font size, weight, family, color, line height, and letter spacing. Description text is editable per segment with template variable support.

The default is usually 0; add top padding to separate the description from the subtitle above, or side padding to keep multi-line text off the screen edges. Comfortable spacing makes longer copy easy to read, which keeps visitors absorbing your value and tapping through.

fields.label: Style the step image
fields.description: Controls how each step's image looks: how it scales (fill = cover the box and crop overflow, fit = show the whole image with possible gaps, crop, or tile to repeat), corner rounding, width and height, and tile repeat. Use fit for logos or illustrations you don't want cropped, and fill for photos that should fully cover the box. This appears only for the Image First or Chart First layouts and is hidden for the orbital Circle layout.

leaves.label: Corner radius
