fields.label: Space around the image
fields.description: Sets the empty space, in pixels, on each side of the step image: top, right, bottom, left. The default is usually 0; add padding so the image does not touch the title or screen edges and sits balanced in its container. A well-framed visual carries the emotional pull on an ad landing page, so adjust this when the image looks cramped or off-center. This control appears only for the Image First or Chart First layouts.

help-block-text-field.title: Text Field
help-block-text-field.summary: The free-text input field — what kind of value it accepts and how typed answers look.

fields.label: What the field accepts
fields.description: Tells the field what kind of value to accept — plain text, a whole number, a decimal, a date, or an email — and automatically applies basic checks plus the right phone keyboard. Use Email for email capture and plain text for open answers. Picking the correct type blocks bad data, keeping any branching, analytics, or CRM that reads this answer reliable.

fields.label: Color of typed answers
fields.description: Sets the color of the text a visitor types into this field; the gray placeholder hint has its own separate color. Pick a color with strong contrast against the field background (use a light color on dark themes) so answers stay legible. Easy-to-read fields are easier to fill in, which protects completion on your data-collection screens.

fields.label: Fill behind the input
fields.description: Sets the fill color inside the input box. Most funnels leave it clear so the screen background shows through, or use a subtle light fill to make the tappable field stand out. Just make sure it contrasts with the typed-text color so answers stay easy to read and people don't abandon the question.

fields.label: Color of the field outline
fields.description: Sets the color of the field's outline, which only appears when the Border Style is an underline or a full box. Use a tone from your theme — an accent or a soft neutral — so the field's edges read clearly as something to tap and type into. A visible outline helps people recognize and fill in the field.

fields.label: Thickness of the outline
fields.description: Controls how thick the field's outline is, from 0 to 50 pixels (default 1). Keep it at 1-2 pixels for a clean, modern look and only go thicker for a deliberately bold style. A visible but restrained outline helps people spot the field at a glance and answer faster.

fields.label: Pick the field outline style
fields.description: Chooses how the field is outlined: a bottom underline under the text, a bottom underline with room for an icon, or a full box around the whole field. A full box reads most clearly as a place to type, while underline styles feel lighter. Your pick here also decides whether the Border Color and Border Width settings actually show.

fields.label: Font for the field
fields.description: Picks the font used for both the placeholder hint and what the visitor types. Leave it on the system font unless you have a brand font, and match whatever the rest of your funnel uses. Consistent type keeps the page feeling polished and trustworthy, which matters when you're paying for the traffic.

fields.label: Size of the field text
fields.description: Sets how large the text in the field appears, from 0 to 50 points (default 15). Keep it around 15-17 points so answers are comfortable to read on a phone. Text that's too small is hard to read on mobile, where most ad traffic lands, and can quietly drag down completion.

fields.label: Weight of the field text
fields.description: Sets how heavy the field text looks, from light (300) to bold (700), with regular (400) as the default. Regular is right for almost every input field. Keeping it regular makes the text read like an editable answer rather than a heading, so the field stays obvious and easy to use.

fields.label: Line spacing in the field
fields.description: Sets the vertical gap between lines of typed text (0-50pt, default 18). It only shows when an answer wraps onto multiple lines, so for normal single-line questions leave it at the default. Adjust it only if you've allowed long, multi-line responses and they feel too cramped or too loose.

fields.label: How the text lines up
fields.description: Lines up the placeholder and typed text to the left, center, or right (default center). Left is the most familiar for input fields and the easiest to scan, while center suits short, decorative prompts. Pick whichever keeps the answer clearly readable for what you're collecting.

fields.label: Override mobile keyboard input type
fields.description: Forces a specific keyboard on mobile devices (Email, Numeric, Decimal, Phone, URL, etc.). Leave as Auto (from field type) to let the system derive keyboard type from Field Type setting.

fields.label: Focus field when screen loads
fields.description: When enabled, the field automatically receives focus and opens the keyboard when the screen appears. Default is true. Useful for primary input fields.

fields.label: Space inside the field
fields.description: Sets the breathing room between the text or icon and the field's edges, on the top, right, bottom, and left. Generous spacing makes the field a bigger, easier tap target and keeps text from crowding the outline. If the field feels cramped on a phone, increase the top and bottom spacing.

fields.label: Space around the field
fields.description: Sets the gap OUTSIDE the field, separating it from the title above and anything below, on the top, right, bottom, and left. Use it to give the field room to breathe within the screen. This is the space around the field — distinct from Internal Padding, which is the space inside it.

fields.label: Set placeholder hint text
fields.description: Hint text displayed in the field when empty, guiding users on what to enter. Can be localized per locale. Styling controlled by text appearance settings.

fields.label: Color of the hint text
fields.description: Sets the color of the faint hint shown while the field is empty, separate from the color of what the visitor types (default is a light gray, #999999). Keep it dimmer than the typed-text color so people can tell the hint from a real answer, but not so faint it disappears against your background.

fields.label: Custom format rule (advanced)
fields.description: An optional advanced rule that forces the typed value to match an exact pattern before the visitor can continue. Most funnels leave this empty and rely on Field Type instead — for emails the Email type already checks the format. Use it only for special shapes like postal or phone codes; if input fails, the Error Message you set is shown.

fields.label: Set validation error message
fields.description: Message displayed when user input fails validation (does not match Validation Regex or Field Type). Shown to guide correction. Can be localized per locale.

fields.label: Fill behind the error text
fields.description: Sets a fill color behind the validation error message that appears when an answer is rejected. Usually leave it transparent so only the red text shows; add a subtle tint only if you want the error to read like a banner. Whatever you choose, keep enough contrast with the error text so the message stays readable and users can quickly fix and continue.

fields.label: Color of the error message
fields.description: Sets the color of the error text shown when an answer fails validation (default red, #FF3B30). Keep it red or another high-contrast warning color so people instantly see that their input was rejected and needs fixing. A clear error keeps them from giving up before they can continue.

fields.label: Font of the error text
fields.description: Sets the typeface for the validation error message shown when an answer is rejected. Leave it on your theme/system font unless you have a specific brand font, and match it to the field's font so the error looks like part of the same form. A consistent error style keeps the screen feeling polished and helps users trust and fix the field fast.

fields.label: Size of the error text
fields.description: Sets the point size of the validation error message. Keep it a touch smaller than the field text (about 12-13pt) so it reads as a secondary note, but not so small it's hard to read on a phone. A legible error helps users spot and fix a rejected answer instead of abandoning the screen.

fields.label: Boldness of the error text
fields.description: Sets how heavy the error message looks (for example 400 regular or 600 semibold). Regular (400) works in most cases; step up to 600 if you want the error to stand out more. Paired with the red color, a bit more weight helps users notice and correct a rejected answer so they keep moving through the funnel.

fields.label: Where the error text sits
fields.description: Aligns the validation error message to the left, center, or right. Match it to the field's own text alignment (left is typical) so the message sits naturally under the input. Keeping them aligned makes it obvious which field was rejected, so users fix it quickly and don't stall.

fields.label: Optional icon in the field
fields.description: Adds a small image — like a mail or person glyph — to the left of the input to hint at what the field is for. It's optional, and you can upload a different image for each language. It only appears with a Border Style that leaves room for an icon, and its size and rounding come from the icon's image style settings.

fields.label: Width of the field icon
fields.description: Sets how wide the icon beside the input is (0-500px). Keep it small, around 20-24px, so it fits neatly next to the text, and usually match it to the icon height for a clean square glyph. Oversized icons crowd the field and make the input look heavier than it needs to.

fields.label: Height of the field icon
fields.description: Sets how tall the icon beside the input is (0-500px). Keep it around 20-24px so it lines up with the text, and usually match it to the icon width so the glyph stays square and undistorted. A right-sized icon reads as a helpful cue rather than visual clutter.

fields.label: How the icon fills its space
fields.description: Controls how the icon sits inside its box: Fit keeps the whole image visible and may leave a little padding, Fill keeps proportions but crops the edges, and Stretch fills the box and can distort the image. Use Fit for logos and glyphs — it's the safe default — unless you specifically want a cropped or stretched look.

fields.label: Rounding the icon corners
fields.description: Rounds the corners of the icon image (0-50px, default 0 for square). Leave it at 0 for normal line or glyph icons; raise it only for a photo or avatar-style icon you want to soften or make circular. It has little visible effect on transparent line icons, so most fields can skip it.

fields.label: Gap between icon and text
fields.description: Sets the horizontal space between the field's icon and the text the visitor types (default 8 pixels). The default works for most fields — nudge it up a little if the icon and text feel cramped, or down for a tighter look. The goal is an icon and placeholder that sit comfortably balanced.

help-content-hero-basic.title: Content
help-content-hero-basic.summary: The headline, subtitle, and optional hero image — the words and lead visual that carry the screen.

fields.label: Your main headline
fields.description: The title is the biggest, first thing a visitor reads, so it carries most of the weight on whether they keep going. Turn it on, then write one short benefit-led line, like an ad headline rather than a sentence. Type @ to drop in an earlier answer (for example @user_goal) so it feels personal, and style it under the gear icon below.

fields.label: Write the headline text
fields.description: This is where you type the actual headline; keep it short and benefit-driven. Type @ to pull in a visitor's earlier answer (such as @user_goal) for personalization, add a link inside the text with @link, or insert a countdown with @countdown to create urgency on offer screens. If your funnel runs in more than one language, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

fields.label: Title look and emphasis
fields.description: Override how the headline looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and an optional highlight behind the text. By default it inherits your project theme, which keeps every screen consistent, so most funnels never need to touch this. Override only when one screen needs extra punch, like a bigger color headline on your hero.

leaves.label: Text background color
leaves.description: An optional fill drawn behind the title text (a highlight pill). Off unless you set it; leave empty for plain text on the screen background.

leaves.label: Font family
leaves.description: The typeface of the title.

leaves.label: Line height
leaves.description: Vertical spacing between lines of text — raise it to give multi-line text more breathing room.

leaves.label: Font size
leaves.description: Text size of the title in pixels.

leaves.label: Font weight
leaves.description: How bold the text is, from Thin through Bold to Black.

leaves.label: Text color
leaves.description: The color of the title text. Keep enough contrast with the background that it stays readable.

leaves.label: Text align
leaves.description: Horizontal alignment of the text: start (left), center, or end (right).

leaves.label: Strikethrough color
leaves.description: Color of a line-through decoration when the text is struck out (for example, an old price).

leaves.label: Background opacity
leaves.description: How see-through the text background fill is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid). Only matters when a background color is set.

leaves.label: Background radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding (px) of the text background fill; higher is softer.

fields.label: Space around the title
fields.description: Adds empty space on each side of the title (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't cramped against the screen edges or the text below. Leave it at the theme default unless the title feels too tight or too far from the next element. Increase a side to give it room, or decrease to pull elements closer together.

fields.label: The line under your title
fields.description: The subtitle is the supporting line beneath your title; use it to expand the promise, add proof, or hint at what happens next. Turn it on and keep it to one short sentence; it shows smaller and lighter than the title by default so the headline stays dominant. Like the title, you can personalize it with @ variables. Skip it on screens where the title already says everything.

fields.label: Write the subtitle text
fields.description: Type the supporting line that sits under your title here, one short sentence that reinforces the offer or tells the visitor what comes next. The same shortcuts work as in the title: type @ to insert an earlier answer, @link to add a clickable link, or @countdown for urgency. If your funnel is multilingual, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

fields.label: Subtitle look and emphasis
fields.description: Change how the subtitle looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and an optional background — styled separately from the title so you can tune each one. By default it inherits your theme (usually smaller and lighter than the title), which works for most funnels. Override only when a specific screen needs different emphasis.

leaves.label: Text background color
leaves.description: An optional fill drawn behind the subtitle text (a highlight pill). Off unless you set it; leave empty for plain text on the screen background.

leaves.label: Font family
leaves.description: The typeface of the subtitle.

leaves.label: Line height
leaves.description: Vertical spacing between lines of text — raise it to give multi-line text more breathing room.

leaves.label: Font size
leaves.description: Text size of the subtitle in pixels.

leaves.label: Font weight
leaves.description: How bold the text is, from Thin through Bold to Black.

leaves.label: Text color
leaves.description: The color of the subtitle text. Keep enough contrast with the background that it stays readable.

leaves.label: Text align
leaves.description: Horizontal alignment of the text: start (left), center, or end (right).

leaves.label: Strikethrough color
leaves.description: Color of a line-through decoration when the text is struck out (for example, an old price).

leaves.label: Background opacity
leaves.description: How see-through the text background fill is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid). Only matters when a background color is set.

leaves.label: Background radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding (px) of the text background fill; higher is softer.

fields.label: Space around the subtitle
fields.description: Adds empty space on each side of the subtitle, controlling the gap above it (to the title) and below it (to what follows). Leave it at the theme default unless the subtitle feels crowded. Increase the top value to separate it from the title, or reduce spacing to tighten the whole headline group.

fields.label: The featured image up top
fields.description: The hero is the large featured image at the top of a headline or wheel-picker screen, the picture that sells the screen at a glance. Turn it on, then upload a file or paste an image URL. Pick a high-quality, on-message visual (product, result, or lifestyle shot); on a paid landing page it is often the first thing a visitor sees. Sizing and position are set just below.

fields.label: The hero image itself
fields.description: Pick the actual hero image: upload a file from your computer or paste a direct image URL, then check the preview thumbnail. Use a high-resolution JPG or PNG so it stays crisp on large screens — uploads are optimized automatically for fast loading. To change it later, just upload or paste a new source here.

fields.label: How the image fills its box
fields.description: Sets how your image fits its box: Aspect Fit shows the whole image with no cropping (you may see empty bars at the sides), Aspect Fill crops the edges so it fully covers the box, Scale to Fill stretches it (can look distorted, avoid for photos), and Tile repeats it as a pattern. Default is Aspect Fit, which never distorts; switch to Aspect Fill when you want it edge-to-edge and don't mind some cropping.

fields.label: Fixed image width
fields.description: Optionally pin the hero image to a set width with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty in most cases — the image then sizes to the screen and stays responsive across devices, which almost always looks best on a landing page. Set a fixed width only when you need the image smaller than full-width or aligned to a specific size.

fields.label: Fixed image height
fields.description: Optionally pin the hero image to a set height with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty to let the image keep its natural proportions from the width — best for most screens. Use a fixed height when you want a consistent banner size; to size by screen proportion instead, use 'Image height relative to container' below, which takes priority over this value.

fields.label: Size the image by screen
fields.description: Sizes the hero image as a percentage of the screen height (0 to 100%), so it scales with the device, the more responsive way to size a hero. If set, it overrides any fixed height above. A common starting point is 30 to 50% for a prominent banner that still leaves room for your title and button below; leave it empty to size by proportions instead.

fields.label: How rounded the image is
fields.description: Rounds all four corners of the hero image; 0 is sharp and higher values (up to 50) make them softer and more rounded. The default is 0. A small radius around 8 to 16 gives a modern, friendly look; match it to the rounding used elsewhere in your funnel, like buttons and cards, so the page feels consistent.

fields.label: Space around the image
fields.description: Adds empty space on each side of the hero image (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't flush against the screen edges or crammed next to the title. Leave it at the theme default in most cases. Increase a side when the image feels too tight against nearby content, or reduce it for a full-bleed, edge-to-edge look.

help-block-roller.title: Roller
help-block-roller.summary: A spinning wheel picker — the data type, the wheels and their values (text lists or number ranges), the selected-value label styling, and the picker container’s background, borders, corner radius and padding.

fields.label: Text choices or numbers
fields.description: Chooses what the picker collects: String for text choices, which allows up to 5 side-by-side wheels (such as month / day / year), or Integer for a single numeric range (such as age or quantity). Set this first — it limits Integer to one wheel, unlocks up to five wheels for String, and changes how each wheel's options are set up below.

fields.label: Joiner between wheel values
fields.description: The character or characters used to join selections from multiple wheels into one combined value — for example '/' turns two wheels into 'Large/Red', or a space joins them with a gap. This only matters when you have more than one wheel; leave it as-is for a single-wheel picker. Choose a separator that reads naturally in the answer you'll store and reuse later in the funnel.

fields.label: Add and set up wheels
fields.description: The spinning wheels users scroll to make their choice. Each wheel is either a List of text options or a Range of numbers; use Add Wheel to add more (up to 5 with the String data type, only 1 with Integer), then expand a wheel to set its type, options, and starting value. Each wheel's selection is saved as a variable you can reuse later for personalized copy or to route users down different paths.

fields.label: List of options or number range
fields.description: Sets how this wheel's values are built: List means you type each option yourself (sizes, labels, months), while Range means you set a from/to span and the wheel fills in every number between, such as 1 to 10. Use List for arbitrary text choices and Range for evenly-spaced numbers. Note that switching between them clears the options you've already entered for this wheel.

fields.label: Edit the wheel's choices
fields.description: The text choices shown on a List-mode wheel. Add, edit, drag to reorder, or delete options (1-20 allowed). The order here is the order users scroll through, so place the most common choices near the top where the starting value lands. Each option is per-language, so translate them if your funnel runs in more than one language.

fields.label: Lowest number on the wheel
fields.description: The smallest number a Range-mode wheel starts at. Together with the 'to' value it sets the span users can scroll — for example from 1 to 10 lets them pick any number from 1 through 10. Keep this lower than 'to', and set it to the smallest realistic answer for your question, such as a minimum age or quantity.

fields.label: Highest number on the wheel
fields.description: The largest number a Range-mode wheel ends at. Together with the 'from' value it sets the span users can scroll — for example from 1 to 10 lets them pick any number from 1 through 10. Keep this higher than 'from', and set it to the largest realistic answer for your question so users aren't offered absurd values.

fields.label: Pre-selected starting value
fields.description: The value already showing when the screen loads. For List wheels, pick one of your options; for Range wheels, pick any number within the from/to span. Pre-selecting the most common answer reduces friction and prevents accidental empty or extreme submissions — leave it empty only if you truly want nothing chosen up front.

fields.label: Size of the selection label
fields.description: Text size of the label that shows the user's current choice above the wheels (0-50, default 18). 16-22 keeps the chosen value clearly readable; very small or 0 effectively hides it. Increase it when you want the selection to stand out as a confirmation of what the user picked.

fields.label: Thickness of the label text
fields.description: How heavy the selection label looks, from 300 (Light) to 900 (Black); default 400 (Regular). Use 600-700 (Semibold/Bold) to make the chosen value read as a clear confirmation, or keep it at 400 if it should sit quietly above the wheels. Match it to the weight of your other body text for a consistent look.

fields.label: Color of the selection label
fields.description: Color of the label text that shows the user's current choice above the wheels (default black, #000000). Pick a color with strong contrast against the container background so the chosen value stays easy to read, ideally your theme's main text color for consistency. This affects only the label, not the wheel options themselves.

fields.label: Where the label sits
fields.description: Horizontal position of the selection label within its container: left, center, or right (default center). Center usually lines up with the centered wheels and is the safe choice; switch to left or right only to align the label with other text or a specific layout. This is purely visual and does not change the value the user selected.

fields.label: Background behind the wheels
fields.description: Fill color behind the spinning wheels (default white, #ffffff). Choose a color that contrasts enough with the screen background so the picker reads as its own distinct card and the wheel values stay legible. A subtle off-white or light tint often separates the picker from the page better than pure white.

fields.label: Thickness of the picker outline
fields.description: Width in pixels of the outline around the picker container (0-50, default 1). Set it to 0 for no border and rely on the background color alone, or use 1-2px for a clean, defined edge. The border color setting below only takes effect when this is greater than 0.

fields.label: Color of the picker outline
fields.description: Color of the outline around the picker container (default light gray, #E0E0E0). Use a light neutral for a subtle card edge, or your accent color to make the picker stand out on the screen. It only shows when the border thickness above is greater than 0.

fields.label: Roundness of the corners
fields.description: How rounded the four corners of the picker container are, in pixels (0-50, default 12). 0 gives sharp square corners; higher values look softer and more modern. Match it to the corner roundness of your buttons and other cards so the whole funnel feels consistent.

fields.label: Space inside the picker
fields.description: Sets the empty space, in pixels, inside the picker container on each side: top, right, bottom, left, between the border and the spinning wheels. The default is usually a small value; increase it to give the wheels breathing room, or keep it tight for a compact picker. A clean, uncluttered picker feels effortless to use, which helps visitors commit their answer and continue through the funnel.

help-options-hero-list.title: Options
help-options-hero-list.summary: The answer choices visitors pick from — selection mode, list-or-grid layout, item states, spacing, and styling.

fields.label: What each choice shows
fields.description: Pick which parts each choice displays — title only, image plus title, checkbox with title and subtitle, and so on; available combos depend on your selection mode and layout. Adding an element reveals its style controls and means you must supply that content (image or subtitle) on every item. Default to title (plus a checkbox for multi-select) and add an image only when it aids the choice.

fields.label: Shuffle item order
fields.description: When enabled, randomizes the order items appear to users on each view. Useful for A/B testing, survey randomization, and reducing position bias in multi-select scenarios.

fields.label: Vertical alignment of items
fields.description: Aligns each choice's content to the top, center, or bottom of its cell. It's most noticeable in grid layouts where cells are taller than their content; center usually looks balanced. In simple lists it has little visible effect, so center is a safe default.

fields.label: Even grid cell heights
fields.description: On a grid, choose whether all cells stretch to the same maximum height for tidy, even rows, or each cell sizes to its own content (giving rows of varying height). Turn it on for a clean, consistent grid; turn it off when items have very different content lengths. Only applies to grid layouts.

fields.label: Unselected item look
fields.description: The default look of each choice before it's tapped — background, border, corner radius, and an optional gradient. Keep it neutral and calm so the selected state can stand out; the contrast between this and the selected look is what tells visitors their tap registered. Pair it with the Selected item look.

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: The fill behind an option the visitor has NOT selected.

leaves.label: Border width
leaves.description: Thickness (px) of the outline around an unselected option; 0 hides it.

leaves.label: Border color
leaves.description: Color of that outline.

leaves.label: Corner radius
leaves.description: How rounded the option corners are (px); higher is softer.

leaves.label: Gradient fill
leaves.description: Optional gradient that replaces the flat background color for a richer look.

fields.label: Selected item look
fields.description: How a choice looks once tapped — background, border, corner radius, and optional gradient. Make it clearly distinct from the unselected look (an accent border or filled background) so visitors get instant confirmation; weak feedback here causes hesitation and drop-off. Your theme's accent color is a reliable choice.

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: The highlight fill behind the option the visitor HAS picked.

leaves.label: Border width
leaves.description: Outline thickness for the selected option.

leaves.label: Border color
leaves.description: Outline color for the selected option — often your accent color.

leaves.label: Corner radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding for the selected option; usually matches the unselected state.

leaves.label: Gradient fill
leaves.description: Optional gradient highlight for the selected option.

fields.label: Padding inside each item
fields.description: The space between each item's edge and its content (title, image, checkbox), set per side — top, end, bottom, start. More padding makes items feel roomy and easier to tap; too little looks cramped. Around 12–16px on all sides reads well on mobile, and the setting applies to every item.

fields.label: Margin around the whole list
fields.description: The outer space between the screen edges and the first and last items, set per side (top, end, bottom, start). Use it to keep the list off the screen edges and aligned with your other sections. This is the outside spacing — for the gap inside each item use Padding inside each item instead.

fields.label: Gap between choices
fields.description: The spacing between adjacent choices — a vertical gap in lists, the gap between cells in grids. Around 8–12px keeps items clearly separate and easy to tap without wasting space. Increase it for a more airy feel, or decrease it to fit more options above the fold.

fields.label: Item title text style
fields.description: Typography for every item's title — size, weight, color, alignment, line height, plus an optional background chip (color, opacity, radius) and padding. It's a shared template, so an edit restyles all items at once. Leave it on theme defaults for consistency, adjusting size or color only to improve readability against the item background.

leaves.label: Font size
leaves.description: Text size (px) of each option's title.

leaves.label: Font weight
leaves.description: How bold the title is.

leaves.label: Text color
leaves.description: Title color.

leaves.label: Text align
leaves.description: Left, center, or right alignment of the title.

leaves.label: Line height
leaves.description: Vertical spacing between title lines.

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: Fill drawn behind the title text.

leaves.label: Background opacity
leaves.description: Transparency of that title background (0–100%).

leaves.label: Background radius
leaves.description: Corner rounding of the title background.

leaves.label: Title padding
leaves.description: Space around the title text (top, right, bottom, left).

fields.label: Item image look
fields.description: Size and look of each item's image — width, height, corner radius, padding, and how it fits its box (fit shows the whole image with possible empty space; fill crops to cover the box). Keep a consistent size and small radius so cards look uniform; choose fill for photos and fit for logos or icons you don't want cropped. Only appears when the layout includes an image.

leaves.label: Image width
leaves.description: Width (px) of the option's image or icon.

leaves.label: Image height
leaves.description: Height (px) of the option's image or icon.

leaves.label: Scale mode
leaves.description: How the image fills its box (fit, fill, or stretch).

leaves.label: Corner radius
leaves.description: How rounded the image corners are.

leaves.label: Image padding
leaves.description: Space around the image inside the option.

help-block-custom-html.title: Custom HTML
help-block-custom-html.summary: The Custom HTML settings for this screen.

fields.label: Keep custom code sandboxed
fields.description: Decides whether your custom HTML runs in a protected sandbox (On, the default) or directly in the page (Off). Leave it On — the sandbox stops your CSS and JavaScript from leaking out and breaking the rest of the screen. Only switch it Off if your code truly needs to reach the surrounding page, and expect to debug styling clashes if you do.

fields.label: Your custom screen code
fields.description: Write the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript that renders inside this custom screen here. Edits stay local until you click Apply to Preview, then they appear in the preview. Critically, your code must call segmentlySDK.navigateNext to advance the funnel and segmentlySDK.getChildSection to read any data sources you've added — without navigateNext, visitors get stuck and never reach your paywall.

fields.label: Editable content for your HTML
fields.description: Adds reusable pieces of content (text, images, and more) that your custom HTML can read by name, so copy and visuals live in the editor instead of being hard-coded. In code you fetch one by its name, which lets you or a non-developer update content later without touching the HTML. The Image URL Scanner can auto-create media sources from external image links it finds, so those images get hosted and tracked by Segmently.

help-block-paywall-header.title: Paywall Header
help-block-paywall-header.summary: The paywall's top bar — an optional close (X) button (its icon color, which side it sits on, and whether it appears at once or after a short delay) and an optional restore-purchases link with its own wording and typography.

fields.label: Show a close (X) button
fields.description: Adds the X in the header that lets people dismiss the paywall and keep browsing. For paid-ad traffic keep it on (optionally with a short reveal delay) — an inescapable paywall hurts trust and can break app-store and ad-network rules. Turn it off only when you deliberately want a hard gate users can't skip.

fields.label: Color the close (X) icon
fields.description: Sets the color of the X dismiss icon (default white; applies only when the close button is shown). Choose a color that contrasts with whatever sits behind the header — dark over a light hero image, white over a dark one — so users can always find and tap it. Low contrast here can leave people feeling trapped on the paywall.

fields.label: Place the close button left or right
fields.description: Puts the X on the start side (left in most languages, right in right-to-left ones) or the end side of the header; the sides flip automatically by language. Default to the start/top-left to match common mobile paywall convention. Move it to the end only when your hero layout needs that corner kept clear.

fields.label: When the close button appears
fields.description: Controls when the X becomes tappable: right away, or after a short timer that lets users take in the offer first (set the length in the delay field below). For ad traffic, showing it immediately or after a 2-3 second delay converts well without feeling like a trap. Avoid long delays that frustrate users or break ad-network rules.

fields.label: How long to delay the X
fields.description: How long the close button stays hidden (1-30 seconds) when you've set it to appear after a timer; it has no effect otherwise. A short 2-3 seconds nudges users to read the offer first without feeling trapped. Longer delays raise frustration and drop-off, so reserve 10s or more only for a deliberate hard gate.

fields.label: Show a restore-purchases link
fields.description: Adds a small 'Restore Purchases' control in the header so returning buyers can recover an existing subscription instead of paying twice. Keep it on: a working restore option is effectively required on app-store paywalls and it reassures buyers, which protects conversions. There's also a Restore link available in the footer legal links, so use whichever placement fits your layout.

fields.label: Edit the restore link wording
fields.description: The text shown on the header restore link, editable for each language you support (default 'Restore Purchases'). Keep it close to the standard 'Restore Purchases' wording so returning buyers instantly recognize it. Add other-language versions only if your funnel actually ships in multiple languages.

fields.label: Restore link background fill
fields.description: Adds a colored background block behind the restore link text. Most restore links sit on the plain header with no fill, so the default is none — leave it unset for the usual text-only look. Set a color only if you want a chip or pill behind the link, then shape it with the opacity and corner-radius fields below.

fields.label: Pick the restore link typeface
fields.description: Chooses the font for the restore link (SF Pro, SF Pro Rounded, SF Mono, or New York; default SF Pro). Match it to the font used elsewhere on the paywall so the screen looks consistent and trustworthy. There's rarely a reason to give the restore link its own typeface, so SF Pro is a safe choice.

fields.label: Restore link line spacing
fields.description: Sets the vertical space between lines of the restore text. The link is almost always one short line, so this usually has no visible effect — leave it at the default. Only raise it slightly if your custom restore text wraps to multiple lines and the lines look crowded.

fields.label: Size the restore link text
fields.description: Sets how large the restore link reads, in points (0-50). Keep it small and secondary — around 12-14pt — so it stays legible but doesn't compete with your headline or purchase button. Restore is a recovery option, not a primary action, so resist sizing it up.

fields.label: Set the restore link boldness
fields.description: Controls how heavy the restore link text looks (for example Normal or Semibold). Use a normal weight so restore stays a quiet secondary link and doesn't pull attention from your purchase button. Bump it to semibold only if it's genuinely hard to read against the background.

fields.label: Color the restore link text
fields.description: Sets the restore link's text color (default a muted gray). Check it against your header background first — that gray default disappears on a dark hero, so use a lighter tint there. Keep it readable but understated so restore reads as a secondary link, with enough contrast to stay accessible.

fields.label: Align the restore link text
fields.description: Sets where the restore link sits in its row — start (left in most languages), center, or end (right) — flipping automatically for right-to-left languages. Usually align it to the side opposite the close button, or center it, so the header reads cleanly. The default works for most layouts.

fields.label: Restore link strikethrough color
fields.description: Colors a line struck through the restore text, but only if you have deliberately added a crossed-out segment to that text. A standard 'Restore Purchases' link has no strikethrough, so leave this alone — it does nothing unless your custom text actually contains a struck-through part.

fields.label: Restore background transparency
fields.description: Controls how see-through the restore link's background fill is, from 0 (invisible) to 1 (solid). It only has an effect once you've set a background color above. Use a partial value for a faint chip behind the text so it stays readable over a busy hero image; otherwise leave it alone.

fields.label: Restore background rounding
fields.description: Rounds the corners of the restore link's background block, from 0 (sharp rectangle) up to 50 (full pill). It only shows once you've given the link a background color and opacity. Use a higher value for a pill-shaped chip; the default of 0 is fine, and you can ignore it entirely if there's no background fill.

help-block-paywall-media.title: Paywall Media
help-block-paywall-media.summary: The paywall's featured image or video — its source, how it fills its area, height, corner rounding, spacing, where it sits relative to the header and body, and an optional dark fade overlay for text readability.

fields.label: Show featured media
fields.description: Turn this on to show a featured image or video at the top of the paywall, or off to hide media and give the plan cards more room. After enabling, choose the media type and upload your asset, otherwise nothing appears. Use media when a visual strengthens the offer; skip it for a tighter, text-only paywall.

fields.label: Image or video
fields.description: Picks whether the featured media is an image or a video. Image is simplest and loads fastest; video can show your product in motion but should be short and auto-playing. Note that switching type clears any asset you already uploaded, so choose first, then upload; picking Video also unlocks the loop option.

fields.label: How the media fills its area
fields.description: Decides how your image or video sits in its space. 'Fit' shows the whole asset but may leave blank bars around it; 'Fill' crops the edges so the area is covered with no gaps. Fill usually looks best for a clean edge-to-edge hero, just keep anything important away from the edges; choose Fit only when the entire image must stay visible.

fields.label: Media height on screen
fields.description: How much of the screen the featured image or video takes up, as a share of screen height. Keep it moderate (around 30 to 45%) so the plan cards and purchase button stay visible without scrolling; too tall pushes your offer below the fold and costs you sales. Always check the result on a phone-sized preview.

fields.label: Round the media corners
fields.description: Sets how rounded the corners of the image or video are. Zero gives sharp edges, which often look best for a full-width hero, while higher values give a soft, card-like look that matches rounded buttons and plan cards. Match it to the rest of your theme's rounding; the default is usually fine.

fields.label: Loop the video
fields.description: When on, the featured video repeats continuously; when off, it plays once and stops on the last frame. Loop short, ambient clips (a few seconds) so the paywall stays lively and eye-catching; turn it off for a video with a clear ending you don't want replayed. This only appears when the media type is Video.

fields.label: Space around the media
fields.description: Sets the space between the media and its surroundings on each side: top, right, bottom, and left. Add padding to inset the image or video from the screen edges for a framed look, or set it to zero for a full-bleed, edge-to-edge hero. The theme default is a safe start; adjust only if the media looks too tight or too floaty in preview.

fields.label: Where media starts vertically
fields.description: Sets where the image or video begins at the top of the screen relative to the header (back button and progress bar). 'Screen Top' starts media at the very top behind the header for a full-bleed hero look; 'Header Bottom' starts it just under the header so the controls stay clear of the image. Use Header Bottom if the header overlaps your media awkwardly, otherwise Screen Top is the most immersive.

fields.label: How media meets the text
fields.description: Sets how the media and the paywall text relate vertically. 'Above Content' keeps the media as a banner with the title, subtitle, and plans stacked below it (safest, always readable); 'Behind Intro Content' layers the title over the media for a magazine-style hero. Start with Above Content; if you choose the overlaid look, turn on the gradient overlay so the text stays legible.

fields.label: Dark fade over media
fields.description: Lays a dark fade over the image or video so any text and buttons placed on top stay readable. Turn it on whenever you layer the headline or content over the media, or when a busy or light image makes text hard to read; leave it off for a clean image with nothing on top. Once on, you can fine-tune its height and color below.

fields.label: Gradient coverage
fields.description: How far up the media the dark fade reaches, as a percentage. A low value shades only the bottom edge (enough for text sitting near the bottom); a high value darkens most of the image. Set it just high enough to cover where your overlaid text sits, leaving the rest of the image visible. This only appears when the gradient overlay is turned on.

fields.label: Gradient overlay color
fields.description: Sets the color of the dark fade laid over your media (default black). Black works best behind white text; choose a dark brand color if you want the fade to feel on-theme. The overlay always fades to clear at the top, so only this base color matters. It appears only when the gradient overlay is turned on.

fields.label: Upload the featured image
fields.description: Upload (or clear) the hero image shown at the top of the paywall. Use a high-resolution image with its subject centered, since the edges may be cropped depending on your fit setting. If your funnel runs in multiple languages you can upload a different image per language; it appears only when media type is Image, and nothing shows until you upload one.

fields.label: Upload the featured video
fields.description: Upload (or clear) the hero video shown at the top of the paywall. Keep it short and lightweight (a few seconds, compressed) so it loads fast on mobile data, and remember it auto-plays muted, so the visual must work without sound. If your funnel runs in multiple languages you can upload a different video per language; it appears only when media type is Video, and nothing shows until you upload one.

You can insert @variables like @{user.name} to echo answers the user gave earlier, which makes the offer feel personal and lifts conversion. Turn it off to hide the headline entirely.

fields.label: Style the paywall headline

fields.label: Benefit checklist
fields.description: The list of benefits below the subtitle, your main proof the offer is worth paying for. Add one bullet per concrete benefit (what's included, guarantees, results), each with a title, optional subtitle, and icon, and drag to reorder. Aim for 3 to 5 punchy bullets, since too many dilute the message. Use 'Add Bullet' to create one, or clone an existing bullet to keep the styling consistent.

fields.label: Style the feature bullets
fields.description: Sets the background color, border, and corner rounding applied to every bullet in the list at once. Use a subtle card background or border only if you want the bullets to read as a grouped card; otherwise the theme defaults look cleanest. Styling once keeps all bullets consistent.

leaves.label: Bullet background color
leaves.description: Fill behind each feature bullet row. Leave empty for plain bullets on the screen background, or set a subtle tint to group each benefit into its own chip.

leaves.label: Bullet border width

leaves.label: Bullet border color

leaves.label: Bullet corner radius

fields.description: Sets the breathing room inside each bullet, between its text or icon and the bullet's edge, adjustable on the top, bottom, left, and right. Increase it if bullets feel cramped, decrease it to fit more on screen. The theme default is usually fine, so tweak only if the spacing looks off in preview.

help-block-paywall-subscriptions.title: Paywall Subscriptions
help-block-paywall-subscriptions.summary: The plan picker — how the subscription cards are arranged, where the selection checkbox sits, the plans themselves, the selected/unselected card styling and spacing, and each plan's name / price / note / billing-period labels, badge, and checkbox styling.

fields.label: Plan card arrangement
fields.description: Choose how the plan cards are laid out. Vertical stacks them one under another, which reads best on mobile and works well for 2 to 4 plans; Horizontal lines them up side by side as compact cards, good for 2 short price options you want compared at a glance. Start with Vertical unless you specifically need a side-by-side comparison.

fields.label: Checkbox placement on plans
fields.description: Choose where the selection checkbox sits on each plan card: left, right, or hidden. Left or right makes selecting a plan obvious; Hidden removes the checkbox and lets the highlighted card itself signal the choice for a cleaner look, but only if your selected style is clearly distinct. Left is a safe default. This also works together with the checkbox styling field below.

fields.label: Subscription plans
fields.description: The list of plans the user can buy. Each plan must be linked to a real product in your connected Stripe account, or checkout will fail when you publish. Per plan you set its four corner labels (top-left = plan name, bottom-left = description, top-right = price, bottom-right = billing period) and an optional badge. Mark your best-value plan as selected by default, since the pre-selected plan converts most often. Use 'Add Plan' to add rows.

fields.label: Unselected plan style
fields.description: How a plan card looks before the user taps it: background color, border, and spacing. Keep this neutral and understated so the chosen plan can clearly stand out against it. The contrast between this and the Selected style is what tells users which plan they've picked, so never make the two look the same.

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: Fill color of an unselected plan cell.

leaves.label: Border width
leaves.description: Outline thickness (px) of an unselected plan cell; 0 hides it.

leaves.label: Border color
leaves.description: Outline color of an unselected plan cell — visible once the width is above 0.

leaves.label: Corner radius
leaves.description: How rounded an unselected plan cell corners are (px); higher is softer.

fields.label: Selected plan style
fields.description: How a plan card looks once it's the chosen one: background color, border, and spacing. Make it clearly stand out from the unselected cards, for example a brand-colored border or filled background, so the user is never unsure which plan they're about to buy. Crisp selected styling removes hesitation right before checkout.

leaves.label: Background color
leaves.description: Fill color of the selected plan cell.

leaves.label: Border width
leaves.description: Outline thickness (px) of the selected plan cell; 0 hides it.

leaves.label: Border color

leaves.label: Corner radius

fields.label: Space inside each plan card
fields.description: Sets the padding inside each plan card, between its labels and the card edge, on the top, bottom, left, and right. Increase it to make cards feel roomier and easier to tap, decrease it to fit more plans on screen. The theme default is usually fine; adjust only if cards look cramped in preview.

fields.label: Plan name vs. price width
fields.description: Sets how much of each plan card's width goes to the left labels (plan name and description), leaving the rest for the right labels (price and billing period). Around 60-70% usually gives names enough room while keeping prices aligned on the right. Lower it if prices look cramped, raise it if plan names wrap awkwardly.

fields.label: Space around the plan list
fields.description: Sets the space around the whole block of plans, between the list and the screen edges and the content above and below it. (Card padding spaces the inside of one plan; this spaces the entire group.) Add space if the plans feel jammed against the body copy or the purchase button; the theme default is a safe start.

help-block-flexible-sections.title: Flexible Sections
help-block-flexible-sections.summary: The build-your-own screen — you stack sections (text, media, product catalog, buttons, lists…) and arrange them: add / reorder / rename / delete, set each section’s size, fill, alignment, border, padding and margin, control whole-screen scroll and padding, and link product-aware sections (for example Text or Purchase Button) to a Product Catalog so labels and purchases follow the selected product. Each section type’s own content and styling lives in its dedicated block article.

fields.label: Add a new section
fields.description: Use + Add to choose what kind of block to place on this FlexibleLayout screen: text, media, product catalog, button, purchase button, list, custom embed, text field, spacer, header, footer, or paywall header. Add sections in the same order a visitor should read them, then drag to reorder if the screen flow changes. Start with the biggest structure first — for example header, hero text/media, products, and CTA — then tune layout settings inside each section.

fields.label: Open screen-level layout settings
fields.description: The gear beside the Sections title opens settings for the whole FlexibleLayout screen, not for one individual section. Use it to control whether the full screen scrolls and how much padding the whole stack has from the screen edges. Open this before editing individual section padding when the entire screen feels too close to the phone edge or when you need a fixed, non-scrolling composition.

fields.label: Let the whole screen scroll
fields.description: When Scrollable screen is on, sections stack vertically and the visitor can scroll through them. Use this for long paywalls, product catalogs, benefit lists, or any screen with more content than fits on a phone. When it is off, the screen uses flexGrow and flexShrink to distribute sections inside one viewport, which is better for fixed hero layouts where the CTA should stay visible without scrolling.

fields.label: Space around the whole section stack
fields.description: Container padding adds space between the phone edges and all sections on the screen. It is different from Section padding: container padding moves the entire stack inward, while section padding adds space inside one selected section. Use container padding first when every block feels too close to the screen edge, then use per-section padding only where a specific block needs more breathing room.

fields.label: Reorder sections
fields.description: Drag the handle beside a section name to change the vertical reading order on the screen. The order here is the order visitors see in the preview and published flow, so keep the persuasion sequence clear: context first, offer/details next, then the CTA. After reordering, recheck fixed-height and flex settings because a section that worked in one position may need different spacing in another.

fields.label: Rename a section for editing
fields.description: Click the pencil beside a section name to give it a clear internal label, such as Hero headline, Annual plan list, or Bottom CTA. This name helps editors understand the structure and is not shown to visitors. Rename repeated sections immediately so it is obvious which block you are opening, especially when several Text or Button sections exist on the same screen.

fields.label: Delete a section
fields.description: Use the trash icon to remove a section from the screen. Deleting also removes that section's content and can affect buttons linked to it, so confirm only after checking the preview and any parent-section links. If you are unsure, rename the section first or move it lower in the order while you verify the layout instead of deleting it immediately.

fields.label: Open one section's settings
fields.description: Click the gear inside a section card to open that section's own settings. The first panel controls the section container — height, flex, scrollability, background, borders, alignment, padding, and margin — and the panel below controls the section's content, such as text, media, products, or button styling. This is the main place to tune how one block looks and behaves.

fields.label: How tall this section is
fields.description: Decides how the section's height is calculated. Auto (the safe default) makes it exactly as tall as its content, which is right for most text and buttons. Fixed lets you type an exact pixel height, and Percent sets it to a share of the screen, handy for a hero image that should always fill, say, the top 40 percent. Your pick also decides which value box below applies.

fields.label: The height number
fields.description: This is the number that pairs with your height mode. With Fixed mode, type pixels (0 to 1000, for example 320 for a tall hero); with Percent mode, type a share of the screen (0 to 100, for example 40). The box is ignored in Auto mode. For a scrollable section, this also sets the visible window the content scrolls inside.

fields.label: Stretch to fill empty space
fields.description: Controls how much leftover vertical space a section soaks up so the screen has no awkward gap. 0 keeps a section at its natural size (the default for text and buttons); 1 or more lets it stretch, and a section set to 2 takes twice the extra space as one set to 1. Raise this on your image or hero section to push the button down to a comfortable spot. Only applies when the section isn't set to scroll.

fields.label: Let it shrink on small screens
fields.description: Controls which section gives up height first when everything can't fit on a small phone. Higher numbers shrink sooner; 0 means never shrink this one. The default of 1 lets sections shrink evenly. Set 0 on must-stay pieces like the button or logo, and raise it on a less important section like a tall image, so the key content survives intact on the smallest screens.

fields.label: Let this section scroll on its own
fields.description: Turn on to let a section scroll independently when its content is taller than the height you set (works only with a Fixed or Percent height, not Auto). Use it for a long list of terms or bullets you want capped inside a fixed window while the rest of the screen stays put. Leave off (the default) for normal sections that just sit in the layout.

fields.label: Which section sits in front
fields.description: When two sections overlap, this decides which one shows on top. A higher number wins; the default 0 is fine as long as nothing overlaps. You only need it when you've deliberately layered sections, like a headline placed over a background image, so give the part you want visible the higher number.

fields.label: Solid color or image behind
fields.description: Sets what fills the area behind this section's content. Solid (the default) uses one color you pick below; Media places an image behind the content for a richer, ad-style look. If you go with Media and put text on top, keep the text readable with a darker image or an overlay so your value proposition doesn't get lost.

fields.label: Background fill color
fields.description: Sets the color behind this section's content, used when the background type is Solid. The default is white. Enter a hex code or pick a swatch, and keep it in line with your theme so the screen feels on-brand, with enough contrast against the text on top to stay readable.

fields.label: Round the section corners
fields.description: Rounds all four corners of the section. The default 0 keeps them sharp and square; higher values (try 8 to 16) give a soft card look that pairs well with a solid background or border to make the section stand out as its own block. The range is 0 to 50 pixels.

fields.label: Outline thickness
fields.description: Draws an outline around the section. The default 0 means no border; 1 to 2 pixels gives a subtle frame that makes a section read as a self-contained card or highlights an offer. Set this above 0 first, then pick the border color below.

fields.label: Outline color
fields.description: Sets the color of the section's outline. The default is black, and it only shows when the border thickness is above 0, so set a width first. Match it to one of your theme's accent colors for a clean, on-brand frame around the section.

fields.label: Top, center, or bottom
fields.description: Pins the content to the Top, Center, or Bottom of the section. It only changes anything when the section is taller than its content, for example with a Fixed or Percent height or a section stretched to fill space. Use Center to vertically center a headline in a tall hero, or Bottom to push a caption to the base of an image.

fields.label: Left, center, or right
fields.description: Positions the content along the section's width: Left, Center, or Right. Center is the usual choice for headlines and buttons, while Left reads more naturally for longer body copy. (Left and right follow text direction, so they flip on right-to-left languages.)

fields.label: Breathing room inside the section
fields.description: Padding is the space inside a section, between its edges and the content sitting in it. Set Top, Bottom, Left, and Right independently, starting from 0. Add some so text and buttons don't crowd the section border or a background image; 16-24 px all around is a comfortable, readable starting point.

fields.label: Space between sections
fields.description: Margin is the gap outside a section, between it and the sections next to it. Set Top, Bottom, Left, and Right independently, using positive values to push sections apart. A negative top margin pulls a section up so it overlaps the one above — for example, a headline resting on a hero image; pair that with stacking order to control what sits in front.

help-block-sticky-container.title: Sticky Container
help-block-sticky-container.summary: A floating bar pinned to the bottom of a Flexible Layout screen so the main button stays visible and tappable while content scrolls — its background bar (colour, opacity, corner radius, outline), the spacing from the edges and around the button, and whether it holds a standard or purchase button.

fields.label: Pin the CTA to the bottom
fields.description: Turns the sticky bar on or off. When on, your main button stays pinned to the bottom and tappable while the visitor scrolls, and the rest of the bar's settings below appear. Turn it on for long or paywall screens so the action never scrolls out of reach (this protects clicks from paid traffic); leave it off on short screens where the button is always in view.

fields.label: Show a bar behind the button
fields.description: Adds a solid bar behind the pinned button and unlocks the background color, opacity, border and corner-radius settings. Keep it on in most cases: the bar separates the CTA from content scrolling underneath, so the button stays readable over busy backgrounds. Turn it off only for a clean floating-button look on simple screens where nothing scrolls behind it.

fields.label: Color of the bar
fields.description: Sets the color of the bar behind the pinned button (appears only when the bar is shown; defaults to white). Match it to your screen or theme background so the bar feels built-in, and make sure it contrasts with the button so the CTA stays the most eye-catching thing on screen. That contrast is what keeps the call-to-action obvious to paid-traffic visitors.

fields.label: How see-through the bar is
fields.description: Sets how transparent the bar's background is, from fully see-through to fully solid (only applies when the bar is shown). Keep it near solid to keep the CTA crisp and readable; lower it for a softer, glass-like look that lets content show through. Avoid going very transparent — if the button blends into scrolling content, visitors may miss it and you lose clicks.

fields.label: Roundness of the bar corners
fields.description: Sets how rounded the bar's corners are, in pixels (default 12, only applies when the bar is shown). The default looks good on most screens; raise it for a softer, pill-like bar or set it to 0 for sharp corners. Match it to your buttons and cards so the bar looks like part of the design rather than an add-on.

fields.label: Outline thickness
fields.description: Sets how thick the outline around the bar is, in pixels (default 0, meaning no outline; only applies when the bar is shown). Add an outline when the bar's color is close to the screen background and you want a crisp edge that separates the CTA from content behind it. Once it is above 0, the border color setting appears so you can style the outline.

fields.label: Outline color
fields.description: Sets the color of the bar's outline (defaults to black; appears only when the outline thickness is above 0 and the bar is shown). Pick a color that frames the bar without competing with the button — a subtle, theme-matched tone usually works best, keeping attention on the CTA itself.

fields.label: Spacing from screen edges
fields.description: Sets the gap, in pixels, between the bar and the top, right, bottom and left edges of the screen. Add a little bottom and side spacing so the bar floats just above the edge instead of touching it. This keeps the CTA clear of the phone's home indicator and gesture area, so the button stays comfortably tappable on mobile, where most paid traffic lands.

fields.label: Space around the button
fields.description: Sets the inner spacing on all four sides between the bar's background and the button inside it. A little padding keeps the button from looking cramped against the edges and gives a comfortable tap target; too much wastes vertical space and shrinks the visible content. Adjust until the button sits centered with even breathing room.

fields.label: What the button does
fields.description: Chooses the pinned button's job: a standard button navigates to the next screen (use it on flow steps like 'Continue'), while a purchase button starts checkout and ties into your paywall products (use it on the paywall). The bar holds one button at a time, so switching type replaces it with a fresh default — your bar styling is kept, but you'll need to re-set the button's label and action.
